articles.title: 244 'mostly Chinese' workers arrested in largest 2026 POGO bust
articles.summary: Authorities raided two Zamboanga Sibugay sites and seized around 3,000 phones.

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 11:04am
The main building of the Bureau of Immigration in Intramuros, Manila as seen in June 2020.
The STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — Authorities have arrested 244 foreign workers, most of them Chinese, in what the Bureau of Immigration described as the country's largest crackdown on illegal online gaming operators this year.

The Bureau of Immigration, National Bureau of Investigation and Armed Forces of the Philippines carried out simultaneous raids on offshore gaming operators, known as POGOs on October 2 in Barangay Kimos in Siay and Barangay Tandiong Muslim in Alicia, both in Zamboanga Sibugay.
At the Siay site, authorities apprehended 113 foreign nationals, consisting of 110 Chinese nationals, two Cambodians and one Hong Kong resident.
Another 131 foreigners were apprehended in Alicia, most of them Chinese, along with nationals from Malaysia, Indonesia and Myanmar.
The immigration bureau said the identities and nationalities of those detained were still being verified.

The foreign nationals are being investigated for alleged immigration violations, including working without proper visas, being undocumented, illegal entry and alleged involvement in illegal POGO-related online activities.

Authorities recovered 78 computer monitors, around 3,000 mobile phones, laptops and cellular SIM cards from the Casa de Coco Pension House compound, along with other technical equipment believed to have been used for online scams.
The immigration bureau said the equipment pointed to an organised illegal online operation at the site.
The government is also investigating possible human trafficking-related offences arising from the raids.

"We will continue to enforce our immigration laws against foreign nationals who violate the conditions of their stay and ensure that the Philippines is not used as a base for illegal activities," immigration chief Joel Viado said in the statement.
The bureau described the raids as "the largest POGO bust of 2026."

Those apprehended will undergo deportation proceedings for alleged violations of Philippine immigration laws. Those issued deportation orders will also be placed on the immigration bureau's blacklist, barring them from re-entering the country.
The Chinese embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to AFP's request for comment.

Ban on POGOs. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared all POGOs banned in July 2024 in his State of the Nation Address. He then formalized the prohibition through Executive Order 74 that November, ordering offshore gaming operations to cease by the end of the year.
He later directed law enforcement agencies to intensify operations against POGOs that continued operating despite the ban. — reports from Ian Laqui and Agence France Presse

articles.title: [Two Pronged] A student needs financial help. What should I do?
articles.summary: Our letter sender, a teacher, asks for help navigating an issue where her student is in need financially

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr. Holmes and Mr. Baer,
I do not know if anyone has ever been in a situation like mine before. I am pretty sure there have been similar cases, but I have not heard of any among my cohorts and fellow professors.

I am a math teacher to undergraduate students. I have been teaching for over 24 years. This year I had a female student (I, too, am female) who I was, at first, angry at. She was always late and, in fact, did not attend the first few days of class because she had not yet enrolled
I once scolded her in public (in a group chat) and subsequently felt so guilty I apologized, also in public, admitting I had no right to single her out that way.
Soon she opened up about how life was so hard at home, about how she needed to work to fund her studies and in fact lived with her aunt while in Metro Manila. Her real family was in Bicol.
Somehow by confiding in me she opened up something that I had never felt for a student before: a certain ”sympathique,” a desire to walk the talk and not just expound on mathematical theories.
Some weeks later, like a bolt out of the blue, she wrote and said she had a problem, was embarrassed to tell me about it. I, of course, encouraged her to do so.

Bottom line. She needs money. But I do not know what for and how much. This really shocked me. I have never been asked such a thing in my life. I have never known any of my colleagues being asked such a thing before either.
I feel I should help her. I do not want to be one of these teachers who tell their students they are on their side and then when they really need help, the teachers back out.
– Pia
Dear Pia,
Thank you for your email.

Cross-cultural issues involving money can be complex and as a foreigner one comes across new examples, such as this one, every now and again. When to give financial support to people who are not family seems to vary from culture to culture. Indeed, in the UK, apart from instances like collections for birthdays/retirements, workplace loans are I think very unusual.
However, there are other considerations at play here. Firstly there are issues around a teacher’s role; secondly there is a power imbalance.

The role of teacher is primarily to impart knowledge as well as provide guidance and support to their students. This is not an unlimited remit; it should relate to the subject/course that the students are studying. Some teachers interpret their role more broadly and offer support beyond the academic, in effect acting as mentors. This is fine provided they remain within the boundaries laid down institutionally as appropriate for relationships between student and teacher.

Support for students can come in various forms and a plea for money can be met even if there is no exchange of cash. Universities often have emergency funds, scholarships, study/work programs, and student affairs offices to help in these situations and helping a student navigate the options is certainly one way of “walking the walk.”

The power imbalance is a slightly different matter. Were you to acquiesce and lend, the student may later feel resentment at the obligation created, you might feel similarly if the money is not repaid, and you risk accusations of favoritism from other students.
All of this distracts from your main job: teaching.

If, despite the foregoing, you decide to go ahead, make sure the amount involved is something you can afford to write off as a simple gift and protect yourself by reporting it to your department head in the interests of transparency.
All the best,– JAF Baer
Dear Pia:
Thank you very much for your letter. I feel Mr. Baer has answered all your direct and open questions about what happened, and more than adequately at that.
What I therefore hope to do is touch on some of what I feel are your unasked questions. Why were these questions not asked in the first place?
There are, of course, as many answers as there are people and also as there are interactions of specific students with their specific teachers.

Let us not try and guess your student’s (let’s call her Anna) motives in wanting to borrow money from you. Instead, let us focus on why the student felt it was ok to try and borrow money from you instead of any other teacher? At least any other teacher of the same cohort, experience, training, etc as you.

That is a worthwhile question in my mind, especially if this happens more than once. What signals are you sending so that a student feels it is ok to ask you more than what your remit clearly states? You are her professor, not her banker.

In my opinion, another worthwhile question to ask yourself is: have you changed in any way? Is this a function of aging alone? Or realizing there is more to teaching than following the letter of the law? Or becoming “wiser” and/or now feeling there is more to teaching than feeding facts (or even better, inspiring the students to get their own facts by learning HOW to think?). Have you opened your mind to the realization that to some, teaching is more than the letter of the description, but also its spirit?

I ask you these questions because of certain things you wrote, but specifically: “Somehow by confiding in me she opened up something that I had never felt for a student before: a certain ”sympathique”, a desire to walk the talk and not just expound on mathematical theories”.
Two Pronged does not have ready answers for you, but this column would definitely be willing to discuss this further with you if you want to.
All the very best,– MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

articles.title: LTFRB receives 356 bus special permit applications for Undas 2026
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has received more applications for special permits amid the expected influx of passengers in this year"s Undas season.

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 10:35am
The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has received more applications for special permits amid the expected influx of passengers in this year’s Undas season.
The agency said it received 356 special permit applications covering 1,003 routes, higher than the 323 applications compared to last year’s Undas break.

“We are reviewing all the data that we have to determine the appropriate number of passenger buses that will be given special permits. The goal has always been to have a sufficient number of buses as a huge number of our kababayan go to their home provinces to honor their departed loved ones,” said LTFRB acting chairperson Greg Pua Jr. in a statement issued over the weekend.

The approval requires bus companies to guarantee their drivers' physical and mental fitness, with the LTFRB warning that operators will also be held liable for reckless driving committed by their drivers.

The LTFRB also ordered Regional Franchising and Regulatory Office personnel to check the status of bus terminals and make sure that the operators would comply with at least the basic facility requirements for passengers.

“We ask the operators to just comply with the commitment they made when they applied not only for special permits but also for operation of terminals. This is a way of respecting and giving back for the trust and confidence of your passengers,” said Pua.
All Saints Day will fall on Sunday, November 1, 2026. All Souls Day, on the other hand, will be observed on Monday, November 2.

articles.title: Peru: Fire burning on road to Machu Picchu kills 1
articles.summary: One person has died and two others have suffered burns in a fire near the main access route to the historic sanctuary of Machu Picchu.

image.caption: The Incas built Machu Picchu in the 15th century Image: Laurent Davoust/Zoonar/picture alliance

blocks.text: A blaze was burning near the main access road to the ancient Inca citadel of Machu Picchu in Peru, leaving one person dead and two injured, officials said on Saturday.
The fire began on Friday in the Sacred Valley of the Cusco region, which also includes the Ollantaytambo train station — the busiest for travelers visiting Machu Picchu.
"We have one elderly person who died in the flames and two others with second-degree burns," Miguel Osco, head of the Cusco Regional Office for Disaster Management and Safety, told RPP radio.
How did the fire start?
Osco said the fire originated from controlled bush burning that farmers carry out to clear land for crops.
The flames spread quickly because of the hot, windy weather and dry vegetation, he added.
The Incas built Machu Picchu in the 15th century.
Located at an altitude of 2,500 meters in the Andes Mountains, the historic sanctuary is regarded as an architectural masterpiece.
UNESCO designated it a World Heritage Site in 1983.
Machu Picchu is Peru's most famous tourist destination, attracting about three million visitors every year.

articles.title: 'Choi-Wan' trough to affect Mindanao, parts of Visayas
articles.summary: Mindanao and parts of Visayas may see scattered rains and thunderstorms.

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 10:07am

Motorists and pedestrians are drenched by heavy rain in Quezon City as the enhanced southwest monsoon (Habagat) continues to batter Metro Manila and neighboring provinces with strong winds and heavy rainfall on August 8, 2026
Miguel De Guzman / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — The trough of a typhoon internationally named Choi-Wan may bring rains over Mindanao and parts of the Visayas on Sunday, October 4, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 5 a.m., Choi-Wan was estimated at 2,585 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon.
The typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 155 kilometers per hour near the center and gusts of up to 190 kph. It was moving north-northeastward at 15 kph.
Mindanao, Western Visayas, Negros Island Region, Central Visayas and Southern Leyte may experience cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to the trough of Choi-Wan.
PAGASA warned of possible flash floods or landslides in these areas due to moderate to at times heavy rains.
Meanwhile, Metro Manila and the rest of the country may experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms.

articles.title: Olafur Eliasson’s ‘Your Curious Journey’ helped me bring the little things back in focus
articles.summary: At some point, I too felt like I was part of the exhibit

blocks.text: As someone who loves going to museums, some of my favorite experiences are those that make me think more deeply, those that put me to a halt and stand in appreciation. I love the moment when a simple visual translates into a story without using words, and shows us a world through the artist’s eyes.

It was that same expectation that I brought with me while visiting Olafur Eliasson’s “Your Curious Journey” exhibit at the Museum of Contemporary Art and Design (MCAD) Manila. Unknowingly, I became part of the art itself as I entered my own curious journey in discovering why Olafur’s works captivated many.

As I took my first steps into the exhibit, a strong yellow light washed over every corner of the space. It felt like a warm yet cold welcome from Olafur as the yellow slowly started fading everything I saw into grayscale, which made the space feel strangely cold and suspended in reality.

“Yellow Corridor” was one of the pieces that amazed me, not just because it primed me for all the changes I was about to experience. It was preparing me to step into another world – one that was unknown, uncanny, and strange.

It was the first time I saw the world in grayscale. While it was fun to see the colors gradually fade as you entered the corridor, it was also scary. Seeing colors disappear, this piece made me think about how, like yellow light, too much of a certain idea, perspective, or action can create a new kind of blindness.

As a nature lover, “Beauty” was one of my favorite pieces in this exhibit. The smell of the water, the sound of the falling mist, and the vibrant colors it projects all tie together into a small waterfall.

This piece made me stand in awe; I could have stood there for hours just watching the installation. It was so simple, yet so effective at evoking a sense of peace, as if nothing else in the world existed. It was a reminder of the beauty of nature encapsulated in a room.

As I moved around the mist, the light turned into a rainbow whose colors changed ever so slightly. Thus, someone standing a few steps away would see something totally different. And to me, it showed how perception can be deceiving and ever-changing for each person.
Personally, this reminds me of a childhood lesson my grade school teacher would say: Put yourself in someone else’s shoes.

There were lots of other parts of the exhibit, but let me tell you about one more that really caught my attention. “Your Uncertain Shadow” is an installation that turns your shadow into different colors and sizes.

It made me feel like a kid again, playing and seeing how my shadow would react. Feeling that childlike spark again as an adult was a fun experience. It felt like a look back to who we used to be, and that’s what this piece did for me.

Contrary to the title of the work, I see this piece as perfectly depicting who we are. We bring pieces of our childhood into adulthood, pieces from friends and family into our daily lives, and memories from the past that taught us lessons to the present. Seeing my shadow split into these colors reminded me of these parts of myself that I often overlook and even forgot. Recognizing these shades of my shadow comforts me, knowing that I still bring the different pieces of me, especially the ones I thought I had left behind.
Olafur’s works made me remember all kinds of lessons that I have overlooked throughout my life. I left with the thought of paying more attention to the little, ordinary things that I usually ignore.

If you’re paying a visit, just remember that “Your Curious Journey” includes installations with flashing lights, colored lighting, darkened spaces, as well as a large wall incorporating moss which may emit a certain scent. MCAD offers free entrance to the exhibit which would only run until November 15.
And if this piece made you curious enough, visit https://www.mcadmanila.org.ph/visit/ for online bookings. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Sebastian Vincent U. Ngo. Basti is a multimedia creative storyteller who focuses on the everyday details that make ordinary moments feel special. He seeks stories and uses design, words, and motion to help people see the familiar in a new light.

articles.title: DSWD provides over P745M worth of aid to drought-affected areas
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development has so far provided P745 million worth of aid to drought-affected areas amid the looming very strong El Niño in the country.

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 9:57am
The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has so far provided P745 million worth of aid to drought-affected areas amid the looming very strong El Niño in the country.
DSWD spokesperson Irene Dumlao said the aid includes family food packs and emergency cash transfer to farmers.
"Nakapag-provide na tayo ng mahigit P745 million worth of humanitarian assistance sa mga lugar na nakararanas na ng mga dry spell tulad sa Isabela, Cagayan," Dumlao told Super Radyo dzbb.
(We already provided over P745 million worth of humanitarian assistance to areas experiencing dry spell like Isabela and Cagayan.)
"Sa Dinagat Islands, nakapag-provide din tayo ng mga food boxes. Parts of Northern Samar, Mountain Provinces, parts of Camarines Norte, parts of Catanduanes," she added.
(In Dinagat Islands, we provided food boxes, as well as in parts of Northern Samar, Mountain Provinces, Camarines Norte, and Catanduanes.)
PAGASA has warned of a possibly record breaking El Niño in the coming months, with less rains expected by October.
The state weather bureau said the El Niño could last until March or even June.
Dumlao shared that the agency continues to produce, preposition and store food packs in their warehouses.

"May mga naka-deploy din tayong mga specialized disaster equipment tulad ng water filtration trucks, water trucks... Pinang-a-augment natin 'yan sa iba't ibang lugar na nangangailangan ng tubig," Dumlao said.
(We already deployed specialized disaster equipment like filtration trucks, water trucks that are augmented in different places that needs water supply.)
Another program of DSWD is the Project LAWA at BINHI, which uses cash-for-work and cash-for-training schemes to help vulnerable communities.

"Sa mga lugar na kami naman ay nag-i-implement ng LAWA at BINHI, kina-capacitate natin ang vulnerable sectors para makapaghanda... Nagtatayo sila ng mga small reservoirs, at nagtatanim ng climate-resilient crops," Dumlao said.
(In places where we implement the LAWA at BINHI, we capacitate the vunerable sectors so they can prepare, like building small reservoirs and planting climate-resilient crops.)
Around 40 provinces are expected to experience lesser rainfall during the dry spell and drought. Once January comes, it is expected that this number could leap to 80. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Chalmers says global economic turmoil will drive budget cuts, but Australia should avoid recession
articles.summary:
Treasurer says ‘very substantial and intensifying pressure’ on federal budget as he points finger at private sector for driving up inflation amid Middle East conflict

  • Get our

blocks.text: Jim Chalmers has warned of “very substantial and intensifying” economic pressures on the horizon but insists he’s not planning for a recession, as he prepares to find new ways to cut the budget ahead of its mid-year update.

The treasurer on Sunday called on critics of government spending to name the services that should be cut, as he points the finger at the private sector for driving up inflation in Australia amid the protracted conflict in the Middle East.
Chalmers said the US-led eight-month war against Iran, which has severely curtailed global oil supplies from the region, has been “disastrous” for cost-of-living pressures.
He also said there was “very substantial and intensifying pressure” on the federal budget.

“No serious observer of what’s going on right now would conclude anything other than [that],” he told ABC’s Insiders. “The longer this thing drags out, the bigger the impact on the global economy and on the Australian economy, whether it’s … on inflation or downward pressure on growth.
“We’re not anticipating [a recession] here in Australia, but certainly it is weighing on global growth, and we’re not immune from that.”
Inflation has jumped to 4% in the year to August, from 3.5%, while the Reserve Bank lifted its key interest rate to 4.6%, the highest figure since 2011.

Chalmers said the government was working on finding further savings to the budget in the mid-year economic and fiscal outlook, due in December, after cuts of $44.9bn over four years were identified in the May budget.
The treasurer said cuts to government spending weren’t the only factor driving up inflation in the economy, and cutting larger sums would impact essential services.

“If people don’t want us to strengthen Medicare, for example, or cut income taxes, or provide cost-of-living relief in other ways, then they should nominate where that should be cut,” he said on Sunday.
Beyond the war’s impact on driving up prices in Australia, Chalmers said the private sector was partly to blame.
“For every $5 of demand in our economy, $1 is public, $4 is private,” he said.
“Budget settings are not the primary driver of prices in our economy. There’s a whole bunch of other things going on.”
after newsletter promotion
But the shadow treasurer, Tim Wilson, said Chalmers should be sacked, claiming his decisions have increased inflation to generate tax windfalls.

“He’s actively stoked inflation, and he’s fundamentally undermined the success of this country, and now he’s announced today he’s on a sort of Argo-style salvation trip for investment, because he’s created a problem of sovereign risk,” he told News24.
The assistant science and digital technology minister, Andrew Charlton, said the consequences of having a recession, which would ease inflation, would be devastating.
“If you have a recession, you throw hundreds of thousands of people on to the unemployment queues, and that pulls a huge amount of demand out of the economy,” he told News24.
“It’s pretty easy to have low interest rates and low inflation if your economy goes through a recession.
“As a Labor government, that is a big priority for us to make sure that we don’t go into a recession that drives a lot of people into unemployment.”
Chalmers will travel to Japan for meetings with business leaders and the country’s finance minister, in an effort to boost investment and improve fuel security.

articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot’s time in Australia being investigated by security agencies after alleged cockpit attack
articles.summary:
Police confirm investigation into period the man reportedly spent in Australia before alleged attempted terrorist attack

  • Get our
articles.byline: Adeshola Ore and Sarah Basford Canales

blocks.text: Australian security agencies have launched an investigation after it emerged that the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound flight spent about two years in the country as a student.

Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625 feet (5,067 metres) in just over 30 seconds.

The United ⁠Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general has said the co-pilot had used a crash axe in the attempted “terrorist attack”, in which the pilot was stabbed mid-air. Numerous media outlets have named the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national.

A source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014, before arriving in the country to commence a university course the following year.
He left Australia in 2017, and his visa was cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed he was no longer enrolled in the course, the source said.
The Australian federal police (AFP) on Sunday said multiple agencies – including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (Asio) – were probing the man’s connections to the country.
“The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man’s links to Australia,” an AFP spokesperson said.
“An update will be provided at an appropriate time.”

US media outlets, including CNN, reported that a now-deleted LinkedIn profile said al-Hammami had studied engineering at an Australian university. Guardian Australia has not verified which university the co-pilot attended.
after newsletter promotion

It came after a British university, Buckinghamshire New University, said a student named Hamam al-Hammami had “previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management” at the institution. It added: “He did not undertake any pilot training at the university.”
A flydubai spokesperson on Saturday said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still ‌under investigation and the airline was not in a position to comment further.

The airline’s flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv have been suspended until further notice after the attack. The Omani co-pilot and the flight’s Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, were taken to the UAE, as it leads the investigation. Officials have said a number of countries including Israel are participating.

The Wall Street Journal has reported that the co-pilot had been barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views. He was then moved to an administrative job at Oman Air, according to the official, before being hired by the UAE-based budget airline flydubai.

articles.title: Brazil's 2026 presidential election is kicking off with polls showing Lula and Bolsonaro nearly tied.
articles.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right populist President Jair Bolsonaro, is taking on incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva. Polls show the first round of voting will likely lead to a…

image.caption: Supporters of Lula da Silva lined the main avenue in Sao Paulo for a final rally on SaturdayImage: Andre Penner/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The latest polling points to a tight race in Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, with leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth non-consecutive term and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro seeking to continue the right-wing populist movement started by his father, Jair Bolsonaro.
The two leading candidates wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday in Brazil's economic powerhouse state of Sao Paulo
Lula vows to 'defeat the far-right'

The 80-year-old Lula capped off his campaign with a tour through the city of Sao Paulo, vowing to "defeat the far right," and framing the election as choice between "democracy and sovereignty" and "barbarism and corruption." Organizers said some 150,000 of Lula's supporters turned up for the rally in Brazil's largest city.
Lula has campaigned on continuing his left-leaning Workers' Party platform comprising welfare programs, state-funded development and income redistribution.

blocks.caption: The 80-year-old Lula is seeking the presidency for a fourth and final timeImage: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bolsonaro's law and order

Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, has served as the Liberal Party's senator for Rio de Janeiro since 2019. On Saturday, he led a motorcycle parade through Sao Paulo's countryside cities of Santa Barbara d'Oeste and Americana.
The right-wing Bolsonaro has campaigned on hardline security policies and tax cuts, emphasizing high cost of living under Lula, who he has slammed as "incompetent."

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro has said he would pardon his father if electedImage: Douglas Shineidr/AFP

blocks.text: "I am convinced ​that everything is in place for us to win this election in the first round," the ​lawmaker said.
He also held up a portrait of his father, while the crowd shouted "mito" — a Portuguese word for "legend" that Jair Bolsonaro's supporters use to refer to him.
Brazil's 2022 election rematch

The elder Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year sentence in prison for attempting a coup to overturn his loss to Lula in the 2022 presidential election. Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to pardon his father if elected.

Lula's team has cast the Bolsonaro movement as a threat to Brazil's sovereignty, pointing to Flavio and Jair's ties with US President Donald Trump, who year slapped a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports in response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch hunt."

blocks.caption: US President Trump had held close ties with fellow far-right populist Jair Bolsonaro [FILE March 2019]Image: Chris Kleponis/CNP/MediaPunch/picture alliance

blocks.text: The younger Bolsonaro has said in interviews he is "more moderate" than his father, who he has said will remain "my compass, my point of reference."
Trump has not endorsed the senator, but has said he is watching the election "very closely."
What happens next?

Brazil finds itself politically divided, and campaigning has been bitter, with online operations from both sides seizing on every gaffe, accusation and rumor, quickly producing slick videos or AI-generated images for social media.

In September, it was revealed Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion tied to the financing of a biopic about his father. He has denied any misconduct.
Who is Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro?
Polls show neither candidate is likely to win more than 50% of valid votes on Sunday needed to avoid a runoff that would take place on October 25.

The latest polling for the first round of voting shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, according to the Brazilian data intelligence and public opinion research firm Quaest cited by Reuters news agency.
In the case of a run-off, the Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Bolsonaro at 44%.
In 2022, Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by only 1.8 percentage points.
Along with voting for president, Brazil's 160 million registered voters are also choosing other lawmakers, governors, and some senators.

articles.title: Ayuda to roads: Where the House wants to add billions in the 2027 budget
articles.summary: Rappler tracks which lawmakers proposed a bigger budget for certain agencies and programs

blocks.text: The House of Representatives’ Budget Amendments Review Subcommittee (BARSC) on Thursday, October 1, recommended P116.32 billion in budget realignments, with social assistance programs and infrastructure projects among the biggest proposed beneficiaries.
The recommendations are not yet final. They still have to undergo deliberation and approval by the House plenary before they are included in the 2027 General Appropriations Bill.

Among the biggest proposed increases are allocations for government assistance programs, including the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) and the Medical Assistance for Indigent Patients (MAIFIP).
BARSC recommended an additional P25.81 billion for AICS and P24.97 billion for MAIFIP.

These programs have drawn scrutiny from watchdogs, including the People’s Budget Coalition, over concerns about their use in distributing government assistance through lawmakers and local officials, including through guarantee letters. The proposed increases also come ahead of the 2028 elections.

BARSC also recommended P10 billion for the Presidential Assistance to Farmers and Fisherfolk (PAFF), another social assistance program that was not included in the original 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).

BARSC also recommended additional funding for infrastructure projects under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH):

articles.title: Senator-judges must learn to contradict presiding officer in impeachment trial - lawyer
articles.summary: The senator-judges should not always agree with whatever the ruling made by the presiding officer amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, a lawyer said on Sunday.

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 8:18am
The senator-judges should not always agree with whatever the ruling made by the presiding officer amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, a lawyer said on Sunday.

“Ang presiding officer is presiding officer only. Kung ang iba mga senator-judges ay may contrary opinion sa sinasabi ng presiding officer, pwede naman nila ilagay 'yan sa boto. Unfortunately, mukhang pinababayan ng ibang senator-judges ang presiding officer, hindi nila sinasalungat,” said Rico Domingo, chairperson of Movement Against Disinformation, in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.

(The presiding officer is a presiding officer only. If the other senator-judges have a contrary opinion to what the presiding officer is saying, they can put that to a vote. Unfortunately, it seems the other senator-judges are just leaving everything up to the presiding officer and not contradicting him.)

Domingo, a former president of the Philippine Bar Association, made the statement after former senator Antonio Trillanes IV held a press conference following the withdrawal of his name as witness in the impeachment trial of the Vice President.

Trillanes also urged Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to prioritize the presentation of evidence over technicalities. The former senator also said that he felt unwelcome after the presiding officer refused to issue a subpoena for him to appear.
“Kung hindi abogado siguro ang presiding officer, eh papasukin nila ang sasabihin ni [former] Senator Trillanes,” said Domingo.
(If the presiding officer were perhaps not a lawyer, they would allow what former senator Trillanes has to say.)

“Unfortunately, masyadong technical ang presentation or the ruling of the presiding officer. Mukhang mayroong kaunting heeding si dating senator Trillanes na mukhang hindi siya papayagan even assuming na siya ay sinubpoena o hindi sinubpoena,” he added.

(Unfortunately, the presentation or the ruling of the presiding officer is too technical. It seems former senator Trillanes has a sense/apprehension that he won't be allowed to speak, even assuming he was subpoenaed or not.)
Moreover, Domingo said Escudero should have allowed the House prosecution panel to present Trillanes as a witness.

“Kung hindi sila tugon sa ruling ng presiding officer, for example in this particular case whether to present Senator Trillanes at that time, sana pinagbigyan na 'yun because after all, after juris prudence ang panel, the prosecution panel, has the right to present the witness at its own, hindi dapat papakialaman ng presiding officer,” he said.

(If they do not agree with the ruling of the presiding officer, for example in this particular case on whether to present Senator Trillanes at that time, hopefully that would have been granted because after all, according to jurisprudence, the panel—the prosecution panel—has the right to present witnesses at its own discretion, and the presiding officer should not interfere.)
However, Senator-judge Panfilo "Ping" Lacson earlier said the decision not to subpoena Trillanes as a witness in the trial did not rest solely with Escudero.

Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol also said it was the prosecution which did not name Trillanes in time for the issuance of a subpoena. He reiterated that despite this, Trillanes still would have been allowed to appear as a voluntary witness. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer
articles.summary: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.

blocks.text: Before the morning rush begins, the sound of praise and worship fills the Neoplan bus station in Ghana's capital, Accra, as a group of Christians gather to prepare to evangelise on vehicles taking travellers across the country.
Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana.
Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.
On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel.

Sometimes they stand in the stairwell next to the driver, at others they walk up and down the aisle reading from the Bible and calling on sinners to repent at the tops of their voices. They do not stop even if the trip lasts for several hours.
The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours.
But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end.
Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both.

The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers.
Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023.

"I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday. There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins. We even heal the sick on some buses," he told the BBC in Twi, a local language.
Wearing a clerical collared shirt, Boateng moves through rows of buses loading passengers before boarding one bound for Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.
We speak to him before the bus departs to avoid breaking the law.
Some travellers listen closely as he delivers his message. Others try to ignore him, browsing their phones, making calls or chatting among themselves.
"Some passengers are very happy with my message. Some even say they have never heard the message in church, but through my preaching they now know it is in the Bible," he says.
The new rules have divided opinion.

Critics say preaching on moving vehicles is a nuisance and a safety risk, as it could distract the driver, while supporters argue that evangelism is a Christian duty and should be protected under the freedom of religious worship.
One woman in her early 30s, who wishes to be identified as Chery Lokko, says she prefers to travel in peace.

''I don't like it because they are a nuisance. Some of them spit saliva on you unconsciously, especially if you are seated not far from them, and they are a nuisance in terms of noise and saliva. I like my peace whenever I'm on public transport.''
In one video widely shared on social media recently, a passenger on a minibus is seen angrily confronting a pastor attempting to board.
"Get down, I say get down," he shouts.
But in this devout country, ranked among the most religious in the world, external, others say evangelism on public transport is an important way of reaching people who may not attend church.
Bernice Nartey, a passenger travelling to Kumasi, says pastors should be allowed to preach, but only with passengers' consent.
"The preaching sometimes helps people to repent. For instance, if someone is going through a stressful situation, the message of the pastor can give the person renewed hope," she says.
Boateng says he was shaken by the regulation and wants religious preachers to be given an exemption.
"We are very worried, because most pastors here depend on preaching to take care of their families through the monetary gifts offered by passengers," he says.
"The government should allow us to preach on the buses and alight when it is exiting Accra," he adds.
For Boateng, preaching is not only a religious calling but also an important source of income.
"I have been able to take care of my children's education. My last-born just completed university, and half of the financial support came from money I got from preaching."
Ghana's constitution guarantees freedom of religion, although those rights are subject to considerations including public safety.
Preaching on commercial buses was first prohibited in Ghana in 2012, with offenders facing up to 30 days in prison.
But enforcement was weak and so the practice remained common, particularly on buses. The new law beefs up the penalties for those that flout the ban.
Preachers using megaphones can also often be seen and heard at Ghana's lorry parks and markets but they are not affected by the ban.

The Christian Council of Ghana did not respond to the BBC's request for a comment but Rev Enoch Paul Hayes, a senior pastor at one of the biggest churches in Ghana, the International Central Gospel Church, tells the BBC he does not think the new rules infringe on religious freedom.
He urges his fellow pastors not to break the law, saying they should find other ways of spreading their message.
"There is social media as an alternative outlet, where the same message can reach thousands of people," he says.
For Boateng and other bus preachers, the new rules create a difficult choice between adapting their ministry, giving up an important source of income, or risking falling foul of the law.

articles.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
articles.summary: Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations of a woman who says she was drugged and gang raped as "deeply disturbing".

blocks.text: Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.
In an eight-minute video statement released Saturday evening, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified only as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".
The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.
She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid.
Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.
Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better".
"We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.
He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".
As part of "broader work" that needs to happen, Kotlikoff said there should be a "serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life".
"Being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility for our own actions, for how we treat others, or for speaking up when someone may be at risk," he said.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled, and has appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead a review of the case.
Kotlikoff said he supported the decision to appoint James to leaddddd a criminal investigation, and welcomed an independent review by a law firm of how Cornell has handled the matter.
Jane Doe said in her lawsuit that she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and could not provide consent.

articles.title: Why Canada is preparing for a (long shot) US invasion
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.

blocks.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion.

Noting the risk was low and the likelihood highly improbable, he told the New York Times he had a responsibility to consider all possibilities as the US-Canada relationship is redefined under the Donald Trump presidency.
"That's just risk management," Carney said.
Trump's global tariffs and his often-repeated desire to make Canada the 51st state has led Canada to war game an attack by the Americans.
In 2025, the US president said it was "highly unlikely" that the US would ever use force against Canada. Instead he said, he would continue to exert economic pressures to obtain political aims.
"President Trump has done more than anyone to protect the great people of Canada," the White House told the BBC in a statement this week.
Military experts who spoke to the BBC also think an invasion is a long shot, pointing to the multiple ways the two countries work together on defence.
But the issue is clearly weighing on Canadians' minds.
In January, after the US captured Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, a Leger poll suggested that over 30% of Canadians believed that a US invasion was likely.

A war between Canada and the US would be complicated and almost difficult to imagine, said Lt-Gen Christopher Coates, a former military officer of 34 years with the Royal Canadian Air Force who held various senior positions.
"I was involved in military operations for my whole career, and we never considered the possibility that there would be a military attack coming from US territory," he told the BBC.
Coates, who had served on Nato missions, noted that Canada and the US collaborate on many aspects of military defence.
They are both members of the north Atlantic defence alliance, which mandates members to defend a fellow member-nation should they be attacked.
The two countries also conduct joint Arctic defence missions under the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD), and frequently share intelligence.
Because of this, Coates said he believes an attack by the US on Canada would not begin with an armed assault, but rather with more discreet means like cyberwarfare.
After World War II, Canada and the US became natural allies for the latter part of the 20th Century, and have become heavily integrated economically, militarily and culturally.

But it wasn't always this way. In fact, a core tenet of Canada's identity is its resistance of US expansionism in the 18th and 19th Centuries, said Tim Foran, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum.
"Fear of the United States is foundational to the political project that is Canada," he said.
Canada was formed as a collection of British North American colonies who remained loyal to the British Crown when the colonies in the modern-day US rebelled.
Before the formation of Canada, the US had attempted to invade British North American colonies, taking control of Montreal in 1775 and nearly conquering Quebec City.

In the war of 1812, the Americans invaded what was known then as Upper Canada, Lower Canada and the maritime colonies repeatedly, resulting in a stalemate. During that war, British troops famously burned down the White House in retaliation.
Foran said that at the time, the colonies that later became Canada relied on Great Britain and its Royal Navy for its defence, as well as indigenous peoples who served as generals in major battles.
Canada again contemplated war with the US post-World War I in response to its growing power and influence.
It drafted a plan that was informed by secret trips to border cities made by Canadian army generals, who would pose as tourists and snap photos of bridges and highways for intelligence.
They also spoke to local residents to better understand their enemy.
A war was an unlikely scenario then, said Andrew Burtch, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum with expertise on Canada in the 20th Century, but the Canadians still wanted to be prepared.
"That's part of what militaries do," he said. "They envisage all sorts of different scenarios."

Even if a US invasion is extremely unlikely, Matthew Schmidt, an associate professor of national security at the University of New Haven in Connecticut, said the fact that Canadians were preparing was a sign of just how drastically the global order has shifted.

He added Canadian leaders do have hard questions to ask about how closely they want to continue working with the American military - a partnership that gives them valuable information should they want to harm Canada in any way.
"It's really doing harm to relationships with the United States, and there's a certain amount of legitimate fear," he said.
Americans might not take Trump's comments about making Canada the 51st state seriously, he said, but Canadians clearly do - and are prepared to defend themselves if needed.
So what would it be like if it happened?
The first phase of a war could be quite short.
According to the model used by the Canadian military, as reported on by the Globe and Mail newspaper earlier this year, a US attack would see Canada's strategic positions overwhelmed within a week
Its military would quickly be outnumbered, forcing Canadian forces to resort to guerilla-type warfare to try to suppress their enemy.
Allied nations like France and Britain would be called on to provide support and defence for Canada, the newspaper reported in January, citing senior government officials.
The theoretical model is believed to be the first time in a century that Canada planned for an American assault.
The modelling is on the lighter end of military combat planning, Coates said.

He said that Canada, unlike its Nato allies, was lagging behind when it came to having a response plan in place in the event of any ground invasion, and that it was now playing catch-up in this era of unpredictable geopolitics.

Part of that, he said, was made evident by a recent call by Canada's defence chief to drastically increase the size of its military, including the addition of as many as 300,000 lightly trained citizen soldiers.
An invasion of Canada might not be straightforward from the US point of view either.
Even with its outsized military, the US would have a difficult time getting buy-in for a fight with Canada, said Schmidt.
"I think you would have a large number of American officers who would resign if given the order to invade Canada," he said.
"They would see it as an illegal and immoral order."
Schmidt said Canadian soldiers and American soldiers routinely train together, and share a mutual respect.

But in the unlikely scenario that relations would deteriorate to the point of combat, Schmidt said the US would likely focus on acquiring valuable Canadian resources like oil and minerals, and political decapitation.
"You would see a a kind of operation that would mirror perhaps what you saw in Venezuela," he said, referring to US military action earlier this year to capture former Venezuelan President Maduro.
Although he acknowledged the US has greater military capacity, he said that "pound for pound" Canadian soldiers would be able to put up a fight.

articles.title: Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup in 1993, dead at 58
articles.summary: Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup with the team in 1993, has died at the age of 58. The Canadiens confirmed Odelein's death in a statement Saturday.

image.caption: The Montreal Canadiens confirmed the death of former player Lyle Odelein, pictured in 2009, in a statement Saturday. (Richard Wolowicz/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Sports
Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup with the team in 1993, has died at the age of 58. The Canadiens confirmed Odelein's death in a statement Saturday.
Quill Lake, Sask., native scored 20 goals, 75 assists in 420 games with Montreal
Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup with the team in 1993, has died at the age of 58.
The Canadiens confirmed Odelein's death in a statement Saturday.
The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette also reported Saturday that Odelein died of a heart attack. He played the last of his 16 NHL seasons with the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2005-06 and lived in the area.
Odelein from Quill Lake, Sask., scored 20 goals and had 75 assists in 420 games with Montreal between 1990 and 1996.
He ranked second in franchise history with 1,357 penalty minutes, and led the team in that category in each of his six seasons with the team.
The seventh-round pick of the Canadiens in 1986 played a career 1,056 NHL games with Montreal, New Jersey, Phoenix, Columbus, Chicago, Dallas and Pittsburgh.
"The entire Canadiens organization is saddened to learn of the passing of Lyle Odelein, who passed away Friday at the age of 58," the Canadiens said in a statement.
"The organization wishes to offer its most sincere condolences to Lyle Odelein's family, friends and close ones."

The Canadiens are saddened to learn of the passing of Stanley Cup champion Lyle Odelein.

News release ↓https://t.co/n2M44SKx7O—CanadiensMTL
Odelein was the first captain of the Columbus Blue Jackets when the team joined the NHL in 2000.
"Lyle is a significant part of our history, serving as our first captain and helping us celebrate our 25th season in March," the Blue Jackets wrote in a social media post on X on Saturday.

"He left an indelible mark on our organization and on our community. On the ice, Lyle was a fierce competitor and a Stanley Cup champion. Off the ice, he was warm, kind and quick with a smile and a kind word. He was a friend to all who knew him and will be sorely missed."
The Penguins also lamented Odelein's passing Saturday in social media posts.
"Lyle was known for his tough exterior on the ice, but we will always remember his generous heart and enormous laugh," the team wrote.

articles.title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
articles.summary: They are accused of selling at least one student derivatives of kratom, often called "gas station heroin" in the US.

blocks.text: A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US.
The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to University of Mississippi students.

US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month.
Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom.

The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release.
Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives.
About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives.
Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said.
Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested.
The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin".
Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form.

For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal. But Kratom is not regulated by the US Food and Drug Administration and is legal in some states, including Mississippi.

The Mississippi prosecutors said that kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances in the US and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine.

articles.title: Philippines voices concern over Myanmar airstrike deaths, injuries
articles.summary: The Philippines, chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), expressed concern over an airstrike in Myanmar's Rakhine state that caused deaths, injuries and destruction, and stood…

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 6:11am

Smoke rises as fire burns following a Myanmar military airstrike, according to a rebel group that controls the area and a local aid worker, in Kyauktaw, Rakhine State, Myanmar, in this screen grab obtained from a social media video released September 28, 2026. Social Media/via REUTERS

The Philippines, chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), expressed concern over an airstrike in Myanmar's Rakhine state that caused deaths, injuries and destruction, and stood ready to facilitate discussions within the regional bloc on how best to assist Myanmar.

"The Philippines is closely monitoring developments and expresses concern over the attacks which resulted in destruction, loss of lives and injuries to those affected," Foreign Affairs Assistant Secretary for ASEAN Affairs Ana Marie Hernando said in an email response on Saturday.
As ASEAN chair, Manila said it remained mindful of the views of all member states and would continue to be guided by the regional bloc's consensus-based approach.
The Philippines said it stood ready to facilitate discussions within ASEAN on ways to assist Myanmar, in line with the common aspiration of finding a solution that is "Myanmar-owned and led."
Monday's Kyauktaw airstrike, Rakhine's deadliest such attack since a December hospital bombing, killed 50 people and wounded dozens more.
Myanmar has been locked in a nationwide civil war since a 2021 coup, with an alliance of armed groups, including the Arakan Army, fighting against the military.
The protracted conflict has since killed around 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million in the impoverished Southeast Asian nation. —Reuters

articles.title: AI giants 'not being nearly careful enough,' warns outgoing OpenAI safety engineer
articles.summary: Days after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence giants, a former OpenAI worker said his industry needs the same safeguards as nuclear power or aviation.

image.caption: OpenAI has delayed plans for a public listing this year due to safety concernsImage: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: A safety engineer who recently quit ChatGPTcreator OpenAI warned Saturday that artificial intelligence (AI) firms were "not being nearly careful enough."
David Robinson's comments come amid growing concerns about AI becoming too powerful — a threat that US President Donald Trump has labeled a "hoax."
OpenAI and Anthropic recently disclosed cases in which their AI models slipped past safety controls, hid mistakes and hacked systems they were not meant to access.
How US, China could end the AI race
What did David Robinson write?
In an op-ed for The Atlantic, Robinson said AI needs guardrails similar to those for nuclear power and aviation, adding, "The time for trial and error is over."
He called for more emphasis on safety and research before US Big Tech develops more advanced AI models "so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster."
Robinson, who oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier AI-model launches, said the recent errors were typical because tech giants are prioritizing "speed and flexibility."
"An environment where things like this can happen is no place to grow artificial minds that could be smarter than we are and that might not do what we want them to."
The former OpenAI employee noted that the firm relies on "iterative deployment." It releases new AI models first and only tightens safeguards after problems show up.
"As ​the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the ​level of care ‌that I believe is needed," Robinson, who worked at OpenAI for 3 1/2 years, added.

blocks.caption: Activists have staged protests calling on AI labs to slow developmentImage: Karl Mondon/AFP

blocks.text: ChatGPT creator insists AI is safe

OpenAI reacted to the latest criticism in a statement, "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage ​and secure, and ⁠we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down."
In recent months, there have been repeated warnings from technology experts and policymakers that AI models are advancing so fast they could take control and possibly wipe out humanity.
Despite those fears, US President Donald Trump is vehemently against stronger regulation, insisting that it will slow down innovation and make it harder for US AI models to beat Chinese rivals.
This week, Trump announced a voluntary safety pact with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet's Google.
The president described the deal as "morally binding,” even if it is not legally enforceable.
He also directed his administration to rename AI as "Super Intelligence" or SI.
A survey by Reuters/Ipsos last month found that three-quarters of Americans worry that AI giants are not doing enough to stop AI from causing serious harm to society.

articles.title: UP, Manila HealthTek sign deal for telemedicine expansion
articles.summary: The University of the Philippines (UP) and Manila HealthTek Inc. have signed an agreement allowing the company to use the RxBox trademark for a biomedical telemetry device designed to support remote…

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 4:33am

The University of the Philippines (UP) and Manila HealthTek Inc. have signed an agreement allowing the company to use the RxBox trademark for a biomedical telemetry device designed to support remote medical consultations and patient monitoring.

The agreement covers the use of the RxBox trademark for a device that measures vital signs and transmits patient data over the internet, allowing healthcare workers in underserved areas to seek assessments and referrals from doctors remotely.

According to a press release, RxBox can measure and record blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, electrocardiogram (ECG) readings, and maternal-fetal data. The system also supports electronic health records, initial patient assessment and referrals to specialists.
UP President Angelo Jimenez and Manila HealthTek CEO and founder Dr. Raul Destura signed the trademark licensing agreement on Sept. 29, 2026, at the UP Manila Museum of a History of Ideas.

The RxBox project previously manufactured and deployed 1,000 units to local clinics in selected local government units, including in the CALABARZON region, where the devices were used to help healthcare workers assess patients and determine whether they needed referral to higher-level facilities.
The units were also deployed to referral centers during the COVID-19 pandemic to support remote patient monitoring and help inform treatment decisions.

Destura said Manila HealthTek is preparing to develop a new version of the device, called “RxBox Next Gen,” with the goal of expanding its use in support of the government’s Universal Health Care program.
“We are celebrating a Filipino innovation that has evolved and continues to find its purpose serving our world,” Jimenez said during the signing ceremony.

The project was developed by Filipino engineers and medical experts, with researchers from UP’s College of Medicine and Technology Transfer and Business Development Office among those involved in its development and technology transfer.
In his speech, DOST Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. said the DOST supported the RxBox project as part of efforts to develop technologies addressing healthcare needs in communities.
“This is Agham na Ramdam — science you can feel. Science that reaches the grassroots, answers our people’s needs, and makes a tangible difference every single day,” Solidum said.
The parties said they intend to continue working with government, academe and industry partners to expand the adoption and commercialization of the technology.

“Let us be relentless in developing this technology. Today, we recommit ourselves until RxBox reaches more communities and until Filipino innovation stands confidently before the world,” de Guzman said. — MCG, GMA News
Follow GMA News Online on Facebook for real-time news and developments in the Philippines and around the world.
