articles.title: Trump urges calls to Arkansas senator in push for permanent daylight saving time
articles.summary:
President appeared to share phone number of Tom Cotton for people to call to push him to support measure

Donald Trump on…

blocks.text: Donald Trump on Saturday put pressure on the US senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas to support a bill to make daylight saving time permanent, urging Americans to call what appeared to be the personal cellphone number of his fellow Republican and the chair of the Senate intelligence committee.

The Sunshine Protection Act passed the House in July, but it faces roadblocks in the Senate, where some Republicans are strongly opposed to it. Proponents, including the president and his administration, argue that the change would provide more daylight during the times that Americans are most active. Detractors said permanent daylight saving time would lead to darker and potentially more hazardous winter mornings when children will be waiting for school buses and parents will be driving to work in darkness.

Daylight saving time is that period between spring and fall when clocks in most parts of the US are set one hour ahead of standard time. Not all states observe it – and under the bill, states can opt out of the change if their respective legislatures act to do so before the bill’s enactment.

“For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill,” Trump wrote on social media, noting that passing the proposal would give professional golfers more time on the greens. “So, everyone in Arkansas … tell Tom to, GET IT DONE! It will be appreciated by all.”
Trump included a phone number with an Arkansas area code. The Associated Press called the number, but no one answered – and the voicemail box was full.
The Guardian also called and was greeted with a message from the service carrier saying, “The wireless customer you are calling is not available. Please try again later.”

Cotton, a member of Republican leadership, reiterated his opposition to permanent daylight saving time in a social media post of his own on Saturday afternoon, though he is not the only Republican who opposes it.

“No one likes changing the clock, me included, but Congress has enacted permanent daylight saving time multiple times before and repealed it each time once Americans experienced absurdly late sunrises in the winter,” he wrote. “Arkansans don’t want their kids going to school in the pitch dark, and I’ll always put Arkansas first.”

Cotton wrote that many Arkansans wouldn’t get sunrise until 8am or 8.30am during the dead of winter if daylight saving time was permanent. In that case, at the height of winter, those in Seattle wouldn’t see sunrise until 9am; and in Williston, North Dakota, the sun wouldn’t rise until nearly 9.45am, Cotton wrote.
But Trump, who is spending the day at his northern Virginia golf club before traveling to Ohio later Saturday, promptly fired back.

“If Tom Cotton were putting Arkansas first, he would give them an extra hour of daylight and, more importantly, they wouldn’t have to run all over their houses, farms, work places, and everywhere else, twice a year, having to change their Clocks, and often forgetting to do so,” Trump said. The president added that he believed “that is really putting Arkansas FIRST”.
This is not the first time Trump has released personal information about a US senator.

While competing for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination, the US senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina described Trump as “unfit for office” after Trump denigrated the military service of the US senator John McCain of Arizona. Trump then released Graham’s personal cellphone number. That prompted a viral video in which the senator dramatically destroyed a series of flip phones. Graham later became a close ally of Trump before dying in July. McCain died in 2018.

A 2025 poll from the AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research shows that if forced to choose, most Americans would prefer to keep that extra hour of daylight in the evening. Only 12% of US adults favor the current system of daylight saving time, which requires people in most states to reset clocks twice a year, while 47% are opposed and 40% are neutral.

Members of Congress have long been interested in the potential benefits and costs of daylight saving time since it was first adopted as a wartime measure in 1942 during the second world war. The Senate passed a bill in 2022 to make daylight saving time permanent, but it stalled in the House.

articles.title: Pakistan vs. Afghanistan: From allies and neighbors to war
articles.summary: For years, Pakistan supported the Taliban in Afghanistan. But now Pakistan is bombing its neighbor. How the former allies became adversaries and why negotiations keep failing.

image.caption: Taliban security forces after a Pakistani airstrike in Khost, September 2026Image: AFP

blocks.text: On Thursday night, Pakistan attacked targets in Afghanistan. The results of that attack are disputed. The Taliban, the Islamic fundamentalist nationalist movement that controls Afghanistan, says that between nine and 10 civilians were killed, including women and children. But Pakistan claims the strike killed 22 militants and destroyed weapons and ammunition depots.
These early October attacks are just the latest escalation in a conflict between the two countries that reignited mid-September, after months of comparative calm.

The conflict was sparked again after a series of attacks on Pakistani security forces. On September 18, an attack on a police compound in the northwestern city of Kohat resulted in the deaths of 31 people and more than 100 injured. A splinter group belonging to the Pakistani Taliban, also known as Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, claimed responsibility for the attack in Kohat, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, bordering Afghanistan.
Pakistan accused Afghanistan of providing the TTP with a safe haven. Afghanistan denies this but clashes at the border and then airstrikes by Pakistan followed.

blocks.caption: Pakistani security officials inspect a mosque destroyed in an attack in the border town of Kohat, September 2026Image: Hussain Ali/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: TTP and Taliban: A complex relationship

The TTP in Pakistan is not the same as Afghanistan's Taliban. Although it does have close ideological and personnel ties to the Afghan Taliban, it is an independent organization that fights the Pakistani state.

Many of its fighters sided with the Taliban during that country's long-running insurgency against international and US troops. This is why, after the Taliban returned to power in 2021, the TTP gained more room and more leverage. This has meant that Afghanistan — a former ally of Pakistan — has increasingly become a threat to its neighbor.
Pakistan has asked the Taliban to take action against the TTP, but the close connection between the two make this difficult.

"Because of these personal connections and networks, it is extremely difficult for the Afghan Taliban to break away," says Conrad Schetter, director of the Bonn International Center for Conflict Studies, or BICC.
How 5 years of Taliban rule have changed Afghanistan

The connections don't mean that the Taliban has any control over the TTP. There are certainly historical connections between the two, but Schetter doesn't believe that equals any sort of strong, direct influence.

"The Taliban are simply not prepared to take orders from Islamabad," adds Thomas Ruttig, co-director of the Afghanistan Analysts Network, a think tank working between Kabul and Berlin. "They won't let anyone outside interfere."
This means the Pakistani policy of supporting the Taliban in order to gain influence in Afghanistan hasn't worked.
Difficult borders

There's also another older conflict that has an impact on the current situation. This involves what is known as the Durand Line, drawn in 1893 by a British diplomat and an Afghan emir to mark spheres of influence between British India and Afghanistan.

The current border between Afghanistan and Pakistan follows the Durand Line and also divides an area on both sides, homeland to Pashtuns, who make up the largest ethnic group in Afghanistan and second largest in Pakistan.
So the border dispute here isn't just about territory, it's also about identity.
"Ethnic and nationalist elements play a significant role in the conflict," Schetter tells DW. Many Pashtuns still refuse to accept the border that the Durand Line created.

In Pakistan, the country's long-running rivalry with India also plays a part. A friendly Afghanistan would have been advantageous for Pakistan. But India has also strengthened its ties to the Taliban.

"While Islamabad once viewed Afghanistan as a source of 'strategic depth' in its rivalry with India, it now increasingly views its north-western neighbor as a liability," an analysis by British think tank Chatham House notes.
Pakistan exerts pressure

Pakistan still has power over Afghanistan, though. As a landlocked country, Afghanistan relies on trade routes through neighboring countries, and Pakistan in particular. Pakistan can use border closures and trade restrictions to exert pressure even as the Taliban regime is trying to reduce dependence on Pakistan and find new economic and political partners.

blocks.caption: A Taliban soldier with an anti-aircraft gun on the border with Pakistan in April 2026Image: AFP

blocks.text: Trade and security considerations are now becoming tangled. Pakistan has held talks with the TTP that were mediated by the Taliban and ceasefires were agreed upon. Talks between Pakistan and Afghanistan also took place. But none of the temporary agreements resolved the crucial question of how to prevent attacks on Pakistan from Afghan territory.

So in parallel with diplomacy, Pakistan has also been relying on economic and political pressure, for example, by closing borders and restricting trade and by sending Afghan refugees back into Afghanistan.

An analysis by the US-based Council on Foreign Relations notes that the Taliban are worried that if they crack down on the TTP too hard, they will drive the group towards another extremist militant group, the Islamic State in Khorasan Province or IS-K. This group opposes the Taliban.

The conflict recently escalated to another level. At the end of September, Kabul reported 28 killed and 32 captured fighters who had infiltrated Afghanistan from Nuristan province, Pakistan. The Taliban accused Pakistan of supporting its armed opponents, something Pakistan has denied.

"It is known from past decades that Pakistan has regularly supported armed groups on the Afghan side — for example, the Mujahideen during the Soviet occupation and later the Taliban," Ruttig points out. "What's new though is that Pakistan apparently also supports parts of today's armed anti-Taliban opposition."
Significant escalation
This is turning the dispute over the TTP into a larger conflict in which both sides accuse each other of supporting armed groups from the other's territory.

British think tank Chatham House speaks of a significant escalation compared to previous border skirmishes. Worryingly, a conflict over armed groups and border incidents is turning into a direct confrontation between the two nation states.
Ruttig believes that it would be possible to contain the spiraling violence if both sides return to negotiations.

"If both sides were willing to return to the negotiating table — perhaps with international mediation —there would be ways to contain the conflict and, above all, to protect the civilian population on both sides," he argues.
Militants kill dozens of security officers in Pakistan

In a late September commentary in Pakistani weekly magazine The Friday Times, Pakistani analyst Saqib Ali Khan advocates for several things that could ease the tensions. That includes a reliable channel between Islamabad and Kabul, a separate approach for armed groups and greater involvement of the population along the border.
The conflict, he argues, is not merely a dispute between two governments but also a security, border, economic and regional conflict.
"Along those lines, there would have to be a shift in perspective on both sides," Schetter concludes.
In the long term, greater economic integration is also needed, he adds, so that Pakistan and Afghanistan do not define their relationship solely through security and power issues.
This story was originally published in German.

articles.title: Tennessee's prison chief resigns after botched execution of murderer Christa Pike
articles.summary: Prison commissioner Frank Strada insisted his team followed protocol, even after two doses of anesthetic failed to kill convicted murderer Christa Pike.

image.caption: Christa Pike was 18 when she killed a fellow student in 1995 [FILE: December 2007]Image: J. Miles Cary/Knoxville News Sentinel/USA TODAY NETWORK/REUTERS

blocks.text: The head of the prison system in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the execution of convicted murderer Christa Pike went wrong, the state governor said Saturday.
Witnesses said Pike was still breathing and moaning after two doses of the anesthetic pentobarbital failed to kill her during Wednesday's procedure.
The attempt was halted and she was transferred to hospital in critical condition.
It was the second time this year that an execution in the southern state had to be halted.
What do we know about the resignation?
Governor Bill Lee said in a statement that prison commissioner Frank Strada would leave his post sometime this month.
Lee said he thanked Strada for "his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment."
In the same statement, Strada acknowledged that: "Stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward."
He said the department had carried out its responsibilities in accordance with established protocol, but called the review "entirely appropriate and necessary."
The state has halted further executions until the review has been completed.
Strada took on the role in January 2023. Nearly two years later, he announced that Tennessee would, from then on, only use pentobarbital for lethal injections of death-row inmates.
What went wrong?
Tennessee authorities have yet to explain why Pike survived.
Her attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.
Pike's lawyers said Friday that she is unconsciousand on a ventilator in hospital.
While they welcomed Strada's departure, her legal team said, “It does nothing to help Christa now.”
"What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," the four-lawyer team said.
"We hope the governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system," it added.
Had the drugs killed Pike, she would have been the first woman executed by the state since 1820.
Pike was sentenced to death in 1996, aged 20, for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, whom Pike was convinced was trying to steal her boyfriend.
Slemmer, who was 19, was tortured and killed in a remote area near the University of Tennessee in Knoxville.

articles.title: Latvia election: Pro-Ukraine PM Kulbergs set to retain power after historic victory for his United List party
articles.summary: Latvia's prime minister looks set to retain power after his party appeared to score the country's biggest election victory since independence.

image.caption: Centrist Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (right) is the favorite, but his coalition is expected to emerge weakenedImage: Wojtek Radwanski/AFP

blocks.text: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs appeared set to remain in power on Sunday after his centrist United List secured 35.3% of the vote in the country's parliamentary election.
The result gives United List 42 of 100 seats and puts Kulbergs in a strong position to form another pro-Ukraine coalition.
What do the results show?
With 97% of ballots counted, United List had secured the country's biggest parliamentary election victory since Latvia regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
The party could secure a parliamentary majority with either the nationalist National Alliance or the liberal Progressives, political scientist Roberts Kits said.

Kulbergs, a 47-year-old businessman and amateur rally driver, only came to power in May after the previous coalition collapsed over its handling of incidents involving stray Ukrainian military drones.
Latvia vote shaped by Russia fears

An exit poll put the the populist Latvia First party in second place with 11.3% — nearly double its share at the last election in 2022. It had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority.
Kulbergs said on Saturday night that he would not cooperate with any pro-Russian parties and specifically ruled out forming a coaltition with Latvia First.
Some 1.5 million people were eligible to vote in the country's 11th parliamentary election since independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.

The election, which saw 100 seats in the Saeima being contested by 14 parties using a proportional system, has been dominated by rising living costs and national security concerns in the small Baltic country which borders both Russia and Belarus.

Kulbergs, has only been in office since May after the previous government collapsed over a dispute about Ukrainian drones. Despite his party leading opinion polls, his coalition is expected to emerge weakened as populist parties gain.
Latvia vote shaped by Russia concerns

Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine is seen as a direct threat to national security in Latvia which, like Ukraine, is a former Soviet state with a sizeable ethnic Russian and Russian-speaking minority.
Unlike Ukraine, however, Latvia is a member of both the European Union and NATO.
Riga is one of Kyiv's closest partners and supporters, having committed itself by law to spending at least 5% of GDP on defense – leaving less room for spending elsewhere.
Many Latvians complain of high prices and low wages, the economy is sluggish, the health system is under strain, and emigration and an ageing population remain persistent challenges.

Populist movements such as the Sovereign Power/Young Latvians Alliance and the Latvia First party have attempted to exploit discontent by taking a less stringent line towards Moscow and arguing that a complete economic decoupling from Russia is damaging.
Lessons from Latvia: How to deal with Russian hybrid threats
German Eurofighter jets in Latvian airspace
Nevertheless, no parties are proposing any major deviation from Latvia's clear foreign policy alignment with the EU and NATO.
Indeed, four German Eurofighter jets have been deployed to protect Latvian airspace during the election in response to a request from Riga.
Once ballots are fully counted, attention is likely to shift quickly to coalition negotiations, which could prove lengthy and complex.

articles.title: Ukraine to step up oil attacks as Russia hits Kyiv bridges
articles.summary: As Moscow intensifies attacks on Kyiv and other cities, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to hit Russian energy infrastructure.
articles.byline: Nik Martin, Wesley Dockery, Dharvi Vaid Dhulia

image.caption: A total of eight bridges connect Kyiv's western and eastern banks along the Dnipro RiverImage: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday vowed to continue hitting Russia's oil refineries in retaliation for what he called Moscow's new strategy of targeting major Ukrainian cities for intensive air strikes.
Ukraine has accused the Kremlin of stepping up attacks on civilian targets in recent days, to force residents to leave urban areas of the country before winter.
In strikes over the past two days, Russian forces have also hit two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in the capital, Kyiv.
What did Zelenskyy say?
In an interview with Reuters news agency, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence agencies had uncovered details of a "new doctrine" from Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure ... logistics ... roads, schools, hospitals, to pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities," Zelenskyy warned.

The Ukrainian leader said that Kyiv would "respond in any way (we can) ... First of all, oil refiners: who give money to them [Russia] for this war. But we will not respond, of course, like them, on any ‌civilian objects."
Second Kyiv bridge struck
This week marks the first time Moscow has targeted the bridges across the Dnipro River connecting east and west Kyiv.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Saturday that the Northern Bridge over the river was struck by Russian forces from the air.
In a statement posted on Telegram, Klitschko said two people were injured and the road surface and trolleybus wires on the bridge were damaged.
"Traffic across the bridge from the left bank to the right bank is currently blocked," he said.
Over the past two days, Kyiv's Southern Bridge has been hit several times by a volley of strikes by Russian drones.
The attacks caused traffic chaos, with long lines of stationary cars and buses clogging major roads.

blocks.caption: Cars were stuck in traffic jams on Friday after Russian attacks on the Southern BridgeImage: Gleb Garanich/REUTERS

blocks.text: A total of eight bridges connect Kyiv's western and eastern banks along the Dnipro River.
Russia urges foreign diplomats, nationals to leave Kyiv
Russia's Foreign Ministry on Saturday, meanwhile, warned foreign diplomats and nationals in Kyiv to leave the city, adding that "individuals are knowingly exposing themselves to mortal danger."

"The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation will continue to deliver massive retaliatory strikes," it said, while adding that "responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning."
In the years following its February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Russia has frequently targeted Kyiv with overnight drone attacks.
Moscow has previously denied a systematic targeting of civilians during its bombings.
Putin on a war footing: escalation on all fronts?
Moldova denounces latest Russian strike on Ukraine
Moldovan President Maia Sandu condemned the latest Russian attack on Kyiv and complained about a violation of her country's airspace.
"Its war is dangerously reaching Moldova," Sandu said in a post on X. "5 Russian air attack weapons, including Banderol missiles and drones, violated our airspace and exploded on our soil."
"Moscow is putting lives at risk across Europe and must be stopped," Sandu said.
The Moldovan Foreign Ministry summoned the Russian ambassador and urged Moscow to prevent such incidents.
Moldova is a strong supporter of Ukraine, and its airspace is frequently violated due to Russian attacks on its neighbor.
Russian forces are stationed in the Moldovan breakaway province of Transnistria, raising fears that Moldova could be the next target of invasion after Ukraine.

articles.title: Tennessee’s top prison official resigning after botched execution of Christa Pike
articles.summary:
Frank Strada leaving position as state launches independent investigation into what went wrong

Tennessee’s top prison official is stepping down in the aftermath of the failed execution of…

blocks.text: Tennessee’s top prison official is stepping down in the aftermath of the failed execution of death row prisoner Christa Pike, the state’s governor Bill Lee announced Saturday.

Frank Strada, the department of correction commissioner, will leave his position later in October as the state launches an independent investigation into what went wrong during Wednesday’s botched execution of Pike, according to Lee.
Strada for his part said his resignation would allow that review to move forward in the best interests of Tennessee.

“Serving as commissioner of the Tennessee department of correction has been a great honor, and I continue to believe the department carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol,” Strada said in his resignation statement.

“Even so, stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward,” he said. “I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred.”

Strada handed in his resignation amid intensifying scrutiny of Tennessee’s closely guarded execution procedures after Pike was injected with lethal drugs on Wednesday but survived. She became the first death row prisoner in the US to undergo such an execution attempt and live.

Pike’s attorney Randy Spivey, who witnessed the procedure from inside the death chamber, described what happened as “cruel and torturous”. He said he personally counted seven needles inserted into Pike’s left arm, “one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her”.

Attorneys have alleged that Pike’s failed lethal injection was the fifth “botched” execution carried out under Strada’s leadership in two states since 2022, as the Guardian reported on Saturday, hours before his resignation was announced.

Pike remained unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital as of Friday, according to a court filing submitted by her attorneys. Her lawyers said hospital personnel were trying to save her life and, as of late Thursday, were working to clear the two doses of the execution drug from her system.

Wednesday’s extraordinary breakdown inside Tennessee’s execution chamber has triggered demands for an explanation from people on both sides of the death penalty debate. Besides ordering the independent review into case, Lee has paused the scheduling of executions in Tennessee.
Pike’s attorneys said they believe complications involving intravenous lines caused pentobarbital to enter her body rather than her bloodstream.

“Frank Strada’s resignation does not change the fact that Tennessee is shrouding its executions in secrecy,” Kit Thomas, a death row attorney in the federal public defender’s office in Nashville, said in a statement. “When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known. Strada then oversaw the implementation of a new protocol that ignored the recommendations of the independent investigation and weakened protections leading to a string of problems in Tennessee, including this week’s horrific botched execution attempt and another one in May. Until there is transparency and accountability, botched executions will keep happening.”
Pike, 50, was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of teenage classmate Colleen Slemmer. Pike and her then boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, killed Slemmer at a job training camp in Knoxville.
A pentagram had been carved into Slemmer’s chest.
After the murder, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar and post-traumatic stress disorders, her attorneys said.

“It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” Pike had said in an earlier petition for clemency. “Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone’s child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime.”
Had her execution that day succeeded, Pike on Wednesday would have been the first woman put to death in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: US Coast Guard searches for missing air ambulance off coast of Massachusetts
articles.summary:
The plane was undertaking a medical evacuation from Bermuda with six people onboard when it lost contact

The US Coast Guard is searching for an air ambulance jet with six people onboard that…

blocks.text: The US Coast Guard is searching for an air ambulance jet with six people onboard that lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) during a flight from Bermuda to Boston early on Saturday morning.
In a statement to the Guardian, an FAA spokesperson said that the agency issued a search-and-rescue alert notice for a Gulfstream G-100 at about 1.20am local time on Saturday.

The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers onboard when it departed Bermuda’s LF Wade international airport overnight for the flight to Massachusetts, according to a statement from the Bermuda airport’s operator, Skyport, obtained by the Associated Press.

NBC News reported that the plane was carrying out a medical evacuation in Bermuda, citing a statement from Clarence Togeretz, the director of flight operations at Latitude Air Ambulance, the aircraft’s operator.

“We always get rather concerned when our crew doesn’t report to us in a timely manner,” he told NBC News. “But I will say that again, optimistically and positively, that doesn’t mean that the worst has happened.”

NBC also reported that the Massachusetts port authority, which operates Boston Logan international airport, said the aircraft did not arrive as scheduled. A port authority spokesperson said: “Our thoughts are with those onboard and their loved ones as the search continues.”
The FAA is coordinating with the Rescue Coordination Center and the US Coast Guard to locate the aircraft.
The search area as of Saturday morning was off the coast of the island of Nantucket, Massachusetts, the coast guard said in a statement posted to X.
Air and surface crews have launched in search of the aircraft, the statement added.
Citing a source with knowledge of the investigation, ABC News reported there were no Americans onboard the plane, though the identities of those onboard were not immediately released.
Officials believe the plane rapidly descended 7,500ft before hitting the water, according to the outlet’s source.

articles.title: 4 Canadians aboard missing Ontario-based air ambulance flying from Bermuda to Boston

blocks.text: Air ambulance went missing early Saturday
The U.S. Coast Guard is searching for an Ontario-based air ambulance jet that has gone missing with six people on board while flying from Bermuda to Boston on Saturday.
The Gulfstream G100 jet with tail number C-GRJP is registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, a Hamilton-based air ambulance provider, according to the tracking website Flightradar24.

The company lost contact with the jet around 1:30 a.m.today, said Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude. The U.S. Coast Guard's northeast division said the Federal Aviation Administration also reported losing contact with the jet in the early hours of Saturday.

There were two pilots and two medical staff — all of whom are Canadian — on board. A patient and their relative were also on board. They are not Canadian and were picked up in Bermuda, Togeretz told CBC.
Togeretz said they are staying optimistic that everyone will be safely found.
Air and surface teams are searching for the aircraft off the coast of Nantucket, Mass., the U.S. Coast Guard's northeast division said in a social media post.

The jet's last trip was from Hamilton to the North Atlantic island of Bermuda on Friday evening, according to flight history on Flightradar24. Before Friday and Saturday's flights, the jet had flown within Canada over the past week.
CBC News has contacted federal and provincial authorities for more information about the aircraft.

articles.title: Florida jury finds ex-sheriff’s deputy not guilty in shooting death of Black air force airman
articles.summary:
Roger Fortson was shot by deputy when he opened door with gun in hand after a false domestic disturbance call

A Florida jury…

blocks.text: A Florida jury recently found former sheriff’s deputy Eddie Duran not guilty of manslaughter with a firearm in the fatal shooting of Roger Fortson, a Black US air force airman who was killed inside his apartment after authorities responded to an unfounded report of a domestic disturbance.
An Okaloosa county jury acquitted Duran, 38, on Thursday after about two hours of deliberations. He had faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted.
Duran, who is Hispanic, was an Okaloosa county sheriff’s deputy in May 2024 when he was sent to Fortson’s apartment in Fort Walton Beach where Fortson – originally from Atlanta – was stationed.
Authorities have said Duran was directed to the apartment after a report of a domestic disturbance that turned out to be false.

After Duran repeatedly knocked on the door, Fortson answered while holding a handgun at his side with the weapon pointed toward the ground. Authorities say Duran fired multiple times before telling Fortson to drop the gun. The encounter was captured on the deputy’s body camera.
Thursday’s verdict came after a four-day trial.

One day after Duran was acquitted, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said that Fortson’s family would continue its legal fight and vowed to “seek accountability” through the civil court system for the 2024 shooting.
While the criminal prosecution has ended with Duran’s acquittal, a federal civil rights lawsuit filed by Fortson’s family remains pending.

“Roger’s life and his service will always matter,” Crump said in a statement on Friday. “His family will keep fighting for him, and we will stand with them as they pursue their civil rights case in federal court and seek accountability for the tragic loss of his life.”

Duran was fired from the Okaloosa sheriff’s office after killing Fortson. His defense attorney argued that the former deputy was “doing his job” and said Fortson would still be alive if he had not armed himself before answering the door.

Fortson’s mother, Chantemekki Fortson, told the Atlanta news outlet WXIA she was unsurprised by the verdict, citing the speed of the jury’s deliberations. “They went to deliberate for just two hours,” she said. “So, again, I wasn’t surprised.”
She also said the trial forced her to face details surrounding her son’s death that she had spent the previous two years trying to avoid.
“Now I can’t do that,” she told WXIA. “Like he’s really gone.
“He’s never coming back. He’s never gonna say, ‘Mom, what you doing? Mom, you wanna go get something to eat? Mom, you need do your hair.’ Like I’m never going to hear my baby’s voice no more.”

articles.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution, governor says
articles.summary: Pike survived two lethal injections on Wednesday and is currently in critical condition in hospital.

blocks.text: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is set to resign after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday.
Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada said in a statement to CBS that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two lethal injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence.

articles.title: Shop clerk and son charged with selling illegal kratom after two Ole Miss students die from suspected overdoses
articles.summary:
Aidan Hamilton and Robert Strang died after apparently ingesting kratom product last month

Federal authorities investigating the recent deaths of two University of

blocks.text: Federal authorities investigating the recent deaths of two University of Mississippi students have charged a store clerk and his son with selling an illegal kratom product, prosecutors announced on Friday.

A drug taskforce in Mississippi had previously urged people to avoid kratom, an herbal substance that acts as a stimulant at low doses and a sedative at high doses, after authorities found packages of kratom derivatives while investigating the deaths on 21 September.

It is still not clear whether those substances contributed to either death – but federal prosecutors said both appear consistent with drug overdoses. Two state agencies were working to expedite toxicology reports for the students, the Mississippi governor, Tate Reeves, said in a 23 September statement. The Lafayette county metro narcotics unit said on Thursday that the investigation remained active and additional charges were possible.

Bank records show one of the students, Aidan Hamilton, made multiple purchases in September from a vape, tobacco and beer store in Oxford, Mississippi, where the university is located, according to a federal court filing.

On 24 September, an informant sent to the store by investigators bought kratom-based pills from the clerk, 51-year-old Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, who warned the informant to “be careful taking the pills because people were dying from them”, the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) special agent Michael Dassance said in an affidavit.

Authorities later detained Mosleh and his son, 18-year-old Islam Yahya Mosleh, who was working behind the counter, and charged them each with one count of possession with the intent to distribute a controlled substance.

Attorneys Scott Davis and AE Harlow Jr, who respectively represent the elder Mosleh and Islam Mosleh, said in emails that they had no comment. The defendants appeared on Thursday before a magistrate judge, who ruled there was sufficient evidence to charge them.

Kratom, which comes from a tree native to south-east Asia, is legal at the federal level. But some state and local governments have banned it, and federal authorities have issued warnings about its risks.

Proponents say that in its pure, ground-leaf form, kratom is a safe, natural herbal supplement that can help manage pain, anxiety and depression, and ease the effects of opioid withdrawal. They say the danger is from kratom derivatives, which are often synthetic and can be highly potent.
In August, the DEA banned three kratom-related compounds.
The 25 September affidavit from Dassance, the DEA agent, said one of the banned compounds was listed as an ingredient in products seized from the Oxford store and Hamilton’s room.
after newsletter promotion
Hamilton – a freshman from Englewood, Colorado – and the other student who died, Robert Strang, a junior from Atlanta, were found in different locations, one on campus and the other off campus.

Investigators found opened packages of kratom or synthetic kratom, labeled “Smax”, in Hamilton’s room with some pills missing, according to the DEA agent’s affidavit. A package of Smax was also found in Strang’s room, though the affidavit says he bought it from a different store.

Yahya Mosleh told the informant who went to the store on 24 September to be quiet when other customers came in and pushed the kratom pills out of sight. When the customers left, he completed the sale, according to the affidavit, again telling the informant to be careful.
Eleven states have banned kratom. Others, including Mississippi, have regulated it, in part by requiring people to be 21 or older to buy it.
The city of Oxford, additionally, has implemented its own kratom ban.

articles.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
articles.summary: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

image.caption: Police forces across the UK have stepped up patrols outside synagogues [FILE: October 2, 2025]Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire/empics/picture alliance

blocks.text: Two Iranian nationals charged with plotting acts of terrorism against the United Kingdom's Jewish community were remanded in custody by a court in London on Saturday.
The pair were detained on September 20, the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
The case only came to light on Friday when the two men were charged, just days after another terror plot, which the UK has linked to Iran, was foiled.
What do we know about the case?

Prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court that Rahman S., 34, and Salam ‌A., 36, are accused of carrying out "hostile reconnaissance" on Jewish targets in Manchester, in northern England.
He said the two men planned to use a "homemade explosive device" and had allegedly been in contact with a third party, an Iranian national, most likely operating from within Iran.
The contact is alleged to have given the pair instructions on how ‌to put together a homemade device from chlorine and brake fluid, the court heard.
Luckett said the two suspects had used online resources, including images, plans and maps, to identify and research potential attack sites.
He told the court that the targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and the Heaton Park synagogue, where two Jewish worshippers were killed in a knife attack a year ago on Friday.
The two Iranian suspects had arrived in Britain in small boats that crossed the English Channel from mainland Europe, Luckett added.
One had been granted asylum, while the other's application is still pending, the court heard.
The pair did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey on October 23.
Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator of counterterror policing, said the plot was believed to be isolated and there was no ongoing public threat.

blocks.caption: Heaton Park synagogue was the scene of a deadly attack in October 2025 [FILE: October 2, 2025]Image: Ian Hodgson/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police find no link to RAF Fairford plot

Evans also said the Manchester plot was "not connected in any way" to the suspected terror plot at RAF Fairford last weekend, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said showed "strong indications" of Iranian involvement.
Also on Saturday, police said a dual British-Iranian national, arrested on Thursday in connection with the RAF Fairford plot, was released on police bail.
The 25-year-old was the sixth person arrested and then bailed as the investigation continues.
Police said the five other men held are all British nationals in their 20s and from London.
UK releases air base plot suspects

Police uncovered the RAF Fairford plot when a farmer spotted suspicious white vans near the base early on Sunday morning and called the authorities. Officers found petrol inside the vans, but no explosives.
UK media reported this week that one of the suspects dialled the police about an hour earlier, though that has not been confirmed.
Tehran has rejected as baseless accusations of targeting RAF Fairford, which lies 90 miles (145 kilometers) west of London and has been used by US bombers to strike Iran.
The UK remains on high alert for potential threats from Russia and Iran.
Iran has previously used proxies to commit crimes on British soil, including repeated attacks and plots against Jewish targets, as well as against dissidents.
Antisemitic attacks more broadly have risen sharply since Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023.

articles.title: ICC allows written testimony vs Duterte
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court has allowed the prosecution to introduce as evidence a prior testimony of one of its witnesses against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo
MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court has allowed the prosecution to introduce as evidence a prior testimony of one of its witnesses against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

In a 15-page decision released on Friday, the ICC Trial Chamber III granted the prosecution’s first request to introduce the prior written testimony of the witness identified in the filings as “P-1100.”
“[The Chamber] is satisfied that the substance of P-1100’s evidence and the reports he produced appear relevant to the background and context in this case,” the ruling read.

It rejected the defense’s opposition to the request, saying the witness testimony will not be offered as expert evidence and there is no indication the prosecution will use it to support conclusions beyond his personal knowledge.
“The Chamber notes that witnesses often provide conclusions or opinions while testifying in court as well as in written statements,” the judges ruled.

“Although P-1100’s prior recorded testimony contains some opinion statements, the defense will have the opportunity to question the witness, including to test the basis of P-1100’s knowledge, to probe the foundation for the interpretations he offers and to elicit the limits of what he is, and is not, able to say from personal observation,” it added.
Defense lawyer Peter Haynes earlier objected to the introduction of P-1100’s prior witness testimony, saying it “is neither sufficiently relevant nor probative of the facts in dispute in this case.”

In his original request, ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang described the testimony as “relevant, reliable and probative.” He also said that it would streamline his in-court testimony during trial.
The judges agreed, but noted that the prosecution’s request for two hours to conduct a supplementary examination is excessive.
“The prosecution shall therefore streamline its questioning so as to complete its examination of P-1100 within one hour,” it added.
In its decision, the judges also authorized the prosecution to introduce five “associate materials” into evidence, although it rejected four others.
“This ruling does not prevent the defense from making use of any of the documents for the purpose of cross-examination,” said the judges.
Duterte’s trial is scheduled to begin on Nov. 30.

articles.title: Sara wants copy of ex-cop’s affidavit
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte wants to be provided first with a copy of the sworn affidavit of Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. before being required to face the National Bureau of Investigation to shed light on…

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte
AFP / Jam Sta. Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte wants to be provided first with a copy of the sworn affidavit of Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. before being required to face the National Bureau of Investigation to shed light on the allegations of the dismissed police officer that he delivered cash in suitcases to her and to some members of her family.
In a statement, Duterte’s counsel Paul Lawrence Lim confirmed that Duterte received an invitation from the NBI for a conference at 10 a.m. on Oct. 5 on Gracioso’s allegations.

“However, since no official copy of Mr. Gracioso’s affidavit was included with the invitation, we have requested the NBI for a faithful copy thereof and all its supporting documents, if any,” Lim said.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said they invited the Vice President to give her the chance to respond directly to Gracioso’s allegations.
The NBI will also invite Davao City 1st district Rep. Paolo Duterte, as well as former speaker Lord Allan Velasco and his wife, Rowena, who have not returned from a trip to Japan.
Matibag said the bureau wants to hear their denials and other explanations, particularly after some of those named by Gracioso claimed not knowing him.

“In your letter, you mention an ongoing investigation into allegations made by a certain Mr. Rodulfo M. Gracioso Jr. and request for our client’s statements, documents and records that may help clarify the issues at hand. However, while your letter mentions an attached copy of Mr. Gracioso’s sinumpaang salaysay, none was attached thereto. Consequently, our client cannot provide any meaningful reply to your request at this time,” Lim and other Duterte lawyers Clifford Chua and Kimberly Resurreccion said in their letter to Matibag.

They added that neither Duterte nor her counsels will appear before the NBI on Oct. 5, although they are willing to have their meeting moved to Oct. 8 “assuming our timely receipt of the requested documents.”
“Instead, we respectfully request that sufficient time be given our client and counsel to examine the sinumpaang salaysay and all accompanying documents to be provided her,” they said.

Gracioso, who served as part of Velasco’s security detail, earlier alleged that he also delivered cash-filled suitcases to her brother Paolo and father former president Rodrigo Duterte on Velasco’s instructions.

articles.title: Public urged to save water while supply remains steady
articles.summary: As the country faces what could be a super El Niño, consumers should save water while there is steady supply, National Water Resources Board executive director Sevillo David Jr. said yesterday.

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am

A resident fetches water from a manual pump along Macaraig Street in Manila on October 3, 2026. To prepare for the possible effects of a strengthening El Niño, authorities have urged the public to conserve water while there is still steady supply.
Noel Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — As the country faces what could be a super El Niño, consumers should save water while there is steady supply, National Water Resources Board executive director Sevillo David Jr. said yesterday.
David said the demand for water is high especially during the dry season and they are expecting this as early as this year.
The country is facing a “very strong” El Niño this month, which may extend until the first half of 2027.

“Let’s be responsible in using water. As of right now, the supply is steady and we can give what the people need but it’s good that we trim our water consumption so what we can save will be used for the next months,” he said in an interview with One News.
David said they have issued water conservation measures to reduce the demand for water.
“When the demand is low, it can help manage the supply, particularly in the time when we can’t rely on rain water due to the ‘very strong’ El Niño,” the official said.
“We should not brush off the effects of El Niño, especially on water supply,” he added.
David said they are coordinating with local government units and other government agencies should the water supply go lower in the coming months.
He also discouraged consumers from hoarding and panic-buying water as it affects water distribution and supply.
“We have enough supply. Use your drums to catch rainwater and use it for other daily (activities) like flushing toilets. Using drums can help in catching water that dams cannot get,” he said.

articles.title: Trial verdict on December 16? No timetable yet, senators say
articles.summary: Two senators yesterday denied impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol’s statement that they have set a Dec. 16 verdict date on Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial.

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Sens. Francis Pangilinan and Panfilo Lacson disapproved of Tongol’s tendency to speak on their behalf without consulting them first.
Senate of the Philippines?
MANILA, Philippines — Two senators yesterday denied impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol’s statement that they have set a Dec. 16 verdict date on Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial.

“I have been asked by the media and the public about the schedule of the trial and the verdict date. The impeachment court has yet to formally or informally discuss this and has yet to decide on the timetable/timeline of the trial, more so a verdict date of Dec. 16,” Pangilinan said on Facebook.
The senator said the alleged “verdict date is merely the opinion of the spokesperson.”
“He has no authority to issue his personal opinions on the Court’s behalf,” Pangilinan said.
Speaking to dwIZ yesterday, Lacson said this was not the first time Tongol made a remark that was unauthorized by the senator-judges.
He recalled the time Tongol seemingly admonished senator-judges and reminded them of the sub judice rule when the trial started in July.

Tongol made the remarks in response to Sen. Robin Padilla’s Facebook post discussing the merits of the Article of Impeachment on grave threats, in relation to the Vice President’s livestreamed statement about allegedly contracting an assassin against President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez.
Lacson said Tongol should have better communicated with the other senators.
“I don’t know where he got the date. Even we don’t know the date,” he said.
“That’s definitely not the statement of the impeachment court,” Lacson added.
He said Tongol, as spokesman, should not preempt the senator-judges’ decision on the matter.
Reporters sought Tongol’s reaction on their Viber group with the lawyer, but he has yet to respond as of publication.
Meanwhile, Lacson defended impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero from former senator Antonio Trillanes IV’s allegation that Escudero was blocking Trillanes’ testimony.
He said Escudero’s ruling did not prevent Trillanes from testifying, and that Trillanes is welcome to appear before the court even without a subpoena.

“The presiding officer has been very liberal from the very start. He knows we are keeping a close watch and that we can overrule him. It is not a dictatorial setup where the senator judges are bound by whatever the presiding officer says,” Lacson said.

He said the postponements on Wednesday and Friday were done not to prevent Trillanes from testifying, but to grant the Vice President’s camp’s request for more time to study the voluminous bank transaction reports of the Anti-Money Laundering Council, the next witness on Monday.

articles.title: Gibo: Turn over ‘China money’ evidence to authorities
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro yesterday urged former senator Antonio Trillanes IV to turn over to authorities his evidence relating to his allegations that the Duterte family received about P319…

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on July 29, 2026.
Edd Gumban / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro yesterday urged former senator Antonio Trillanes IV to turn over to authorities his evidence relating to his allegations that the Duterte family received about P319 million in funds from China, in order to facilitate a thorough investigation.
“The allegations of former senator Trillanes, if substantiated, raise serious implications for national security,” Teodoro said in a statement released by Palace press officer Claire Castro.

According to Castro, Teodoro was asked to comment on Trillanes’ claim that the Chinese funds went to Vice President Sara Duterte’s Tapang and Malasakit Alliance to boost the political career of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte.
On Friday, Castro said allegations that the Vice President and her husband received millions in remittances from China cannot be dismissed as the country’s sovereignty is at stake.
At a press conference in San Juan on Friday, Trillanes presented what he described as documents and findings of his research team on the Duterte family’s business and financial ties.
Trillanes said about P319 million in funds from Chinese government and corporate sources entered businesses and a foundation linked to the Duterte family.

He alleged that more than P319 million entered Cale88 Foods Corp., which he linked to the Vice President’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, while another P150 million went to the Tapang at Malasakit Foundation, where Duterte was identified as a member of the board of trustees.

Trillanes also alleged that members of the Duterte family received P181.6 million from businessman and alleged drug lord Sammy Uy between 2011 and 2013. Of the amount, P38.8 million allegedly went to Davao City 1st district Rep. Paolo Duterte, P51.5 million to Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, P53.2 million to Cielito Avanceña for Veronica Duterte and P15.6 million to former president Duterte.
Follow the money

For Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesman on the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela, there should be a deeper investigation into the allegations that certain politicians received financial support from China.
Tarriela pointed out that Beijing is “using its influence to ensure that its own interests will be pushed by its own (supported) candidates.”

“We need to establish the China connection. What if this is true? That is a national security concern if our politicians are accepting hundreds of millions of pesos to be supported by China,” he said.
Tarriela said there is no doubt that Beijing is probably financing politicians, but he emphasized that there should be evidence to solidify the “established facts.”

“We still don’t have very concrete evidence. But if former senator Trillanes can prove how to trace the money – where it came from, how it was brought to a particular politician – then this is the most successful investigative way of proving that China is funding a politician,” he added.
The PCG official flagged the suspicion as some politicians reportedly have close ties with the Chinese embassy and refuse to speak on the issues concerning the West Philippine Sea.
“You can barely hear them criticize the unlawful and barbaric behavior of the People’s Republic of China in the West Philippine Sea,” Tarriela said, without naming politicians.
Tarriela underscored that the 2028 national elections could carve out foreign policy directions to approach the issue in the West Philippine Sea.
“Whoever the president may be, he will be very powerful. The moment he orders us to stay quiet on the West Philippine Sea, we may forget the issues,” he said.
The Chinese embassy declined to comment on the funding allegations, stressing that they do not want to get involved in Philippine politics. — Andrew Ronquillo, Michael Punongbayan

articles.title: Staggered LPG price hike set
articles.summary: Republic Gas Corp. has begun implementing a staggered P18-per-kilogram price increase for its liquefied petroleum gas products, rendering the excise tax suspension futile as global crude prices…

blocks.text: October 4, 2026 | 12:00am
A store helper selling Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) changes the LPG prices on their price board in Paco, Manila on March 25, 2026.
STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — Republic Gas Corp. (Regasco) has begun implementing a staggered P18-per-kilogram price increase for its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) products, rendering the excise tax suspension futile as global crude prices remain elevated.
The LPG firm hiked the price of its products by P10 per kilo yesterday. It will be followed by a P5 per kilo increase on Oct. 10 and P3 per kilo on Oct. 17.
The total hikes will make a standard 11-kilogram cylinder about P198 more expensive.
Regasco president Arnel Ty said the first phase of the increase would raise the price of 11-kilogram LPG tanks to about P1,300 each.
The selling price will still depend on the retailer’s location. Ty said LPG prices in Mindanao are P150 higher compared to Luzon due to transportation costs.
LPG prices have been driven up by both a rise in contract and freight costs in September.
“Saudi Aramco announced that the (contract) price of LPG rose by more than $65 per metric ton, which is equivalent to P5 per kilo in our local prices,” Ty told radio dzBB on Friday.

“Aside from that, the spike in Dubai crude oil prices to $113 per barrel from $90 in the previous month caused shipping costs, which we also call the premium, to rise by P13 per kilo. So, the total increase for October is P18 per kilo,” he added.
Developments in global markets completely offset the P3-per-kilo cut in LPG prices that took effect at the end of September as a result of the excise tax suspension ordered by President Marcos.
Other LPG firms like Solane and Petron Gasul have not yet announced whether they will stagger prices as well.
Supply is also an issue as LPG firms’ main source of stocks – China – suspended fuel exports in October to protect its domestic inventory.
Ty said Regasco currently holds 20 days’ worth of supply, well above the seven-day minimum requirement but far from the 45 days the Department of Energy aspires to.
He said alternatives are available, but they come with literal costs.
“We can get from Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, but their prices are more expensive,” Ty said.
Reuters reported that China did not give its major refiners the green light to export their products other than to Hong Kong and Macau during its weeklong public holidays.
It is unclear whether Beijing will allow fuel exports again after the holidays end on Oct. 7.
Ty hopes that the United States and Iran will restart negotiations after the US goes into the polls for its midterm elections on Nov. 3.

The midterm elections will only determine which party controls the US Congress for the next two years. Polls show Trump’s Republican Party is badly losing to opposition Democrats as high gas prices brought about by the war affect Americans’ cost of living.

articles.title: Woman, 2 children dead after serious collision near Foam Lake, Sask.
articles.summary: A serious car crash left three people dead and four others injured. A 40-year old man from South Carolina was arrested and charged.

image.caption: RCMP have charged a 40-year-old man from South Carolina after the crash. (Charles Contant/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Saskatchewan·Updated
A serious car crash left three people dead and four others injured. A 40-year old man from South Carolina was arrested and charged.
40-year-old man from Sumter, South Carolina, was arrested and charged
A serious collision near Foam Lake, Sask., Friday afternoon has left three people dead.

On Friday afternoon, a truck was attempting to pass a semi and collided with an SUV on a grid road about nine kilometres west of Foam Lake, RCMP said in a Saturday news release. Foam Lake is about 150 kilometres northeast of Regina.
A 40-year old woman, an eight-year old girl and a five-year old girl, all from Foam Lake, were in the SUV and were declared dead at the scene by EMS.
An adult man was also in the SUV and was taken to hospital by STARS with serious injuries, the release said.

The driver of the truck was taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, and two passengers were also taken to hospital. One passenger had non-life-threatening injuries, according to EMS, while the other had serious injuries, according to STARS, the release said.
The semi driver not not report any physical injuries to police and his semi was not damaged.

RCMP say 40-year-old Kelly Knopf from Sumter, South Carolina, was arrested and charged with three counts each of dangerous operation of a vehicle causing death and dangerous operation of a vehicle causing bodily harm.
He is scheduled to appear in Yorkton Provincial Court on Monday.
Wadena/Foam Lake RCMP continue to investigate with the assistance of a Saskatchewan RCMP collision reconstructionist.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Randi LaRocque is a Métis woman working as a reporter with CBC Saskatchewan. She can be reached at randi.larocque@cbc.ca

articles.title: Medical plane with 6 on board missing off Massachusetts coast
articles.summary: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.

blocks.text: US authorities are searching for six people after a medical plane bound for Boston, Massachusetts went missing early Saturday morning.
The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC that it lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane and put out a search and rescue notice just after 1:00 local time (6:00 GMT).
An air and water search is underway off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, according to the US Coast Guard's Northeast District.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was slated to land at Boston's Logan International at 1:30 EDT (6:30 GMT).
According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.
FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

articles.title: TSA to prohibit airport security officers from sitting down while checking travelers’ IDs
articles.summary:
TSA says rule change is meant to keep officers ‘alert’, but union says it ignores safety and ‘common decency’

US airport security officers who verify boarding passes and IDs ahead of…

blocks.text: US airport security officers who verify boarding passes and IDs ahead of security checkpoints will no longer be allowed to sit down while working.
The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) was moving forward with this change in policy to keep officers “alert”, the agency confirmed recently.
“This welcome change reinforces both our security posture and our commitment to hospitality by having these officers on their feet and alert,” a TSA spokesperson said in a statement to ABC News.

“All officers must meet fitness for duty requirements to be capable of performing their vital national security function while simultaneously creating a welcoming and professional environment for travelers,” the statement added.
The American Federation of Government Employees Council (AFGEC), the union representing TSA officers, pushed back on this decision and said in a statement that it was not involved in the decision.

“These chairs serve as basic ergonomic and safety support for officers that stand and walk on hard surfaces all day,” the union added. “TSA is treating this matter like it is a privilege – it is not; it is basic safety and common decency for the workforce.”
Additionally, the union is calling the TSA’s move a “disregard for employee rights and safety”.
“This disregard for employee rights and safety is an example of a broad pattern of TSA’s true consideration of the employees who keep our nation safe,” the union’s statement said.
The TSA has navigated a tumultuous year after withstanding a 76-day government shutdown from February to April that resulted in officers working without pay.
Due to the shutdown, some TSA workers did not report for unpaid duty or quit their jobs – and lines at security checkpoints grew across the US.

TSA workers were finally paid at the end of March after a presidential order from Donald Trump. The government shutdown ended on 30 April after the US House passed a bill funding the Department of Homeland Security.
Furthermore, the labor union is raising alarms over a new program that will expand privatizing security checkpoints at three airports.
The AFGE has been reviewing legal options to fight back against the privatization push from the Trump administration.

As TSA workers navigate the growing changes to the agency under the Trump administration, the union is urging congressional and senatorial leaders to join its “collective resistance” against the administration.

“This is an opportune time to meet with members and non-members alike to tell and show them the importance of joining this union to form our collective resistance against this regime that is literally attempting to take out our workforce through whichever means possible,” it concluded.

articles.title: Women given free cycling shorts to prevent upskirting on Oktoberfest amusement ride
articles.summary:
Investigation revealed thousands of voyeuristic videos taken on Munich beer festival’s Teufelsrad or Devil’s Wheel

Women have been given free cycling shorts to prevent upskirting on a famous…

blocks.text: Women have been given free cycling shorts to prevent upskirting on a famous amusement ride at the Oktoberfest in Munich, after an investigation revealed tens of thousands of voyeuristic videos circulating online.

The Teufelsrad or Devil’s Wheel, which rapidly spins around while people try to sit on it for as long as they can, is one of the beer festival’s oldest rides. But many of the videos discovered by German journalists focus on women whose traditional dirndl dresses have ridden up, often showing their underwear.

The findings have revived concerns about upskirting – secretly filming or taking photos under someone’s skirt without consent, which has been illegal in Germany since 2020. It is punishable by a fine or up to two years in prison. But some women’s rights advocates have said the law is not enough to stop the abuse.
According to the research by the Munich daily newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung, more than 32,000 videos linked to the Teufelsrad were found on Meta platforms alone, some of them with millions of views.

The operator of the ride, Elisabeth Polaczy, told the BBC she has been handing out free cycling shorts to women and girls wearing dresses to protect them from people filming them. She has given out more than 100 pairs during this Oktoberfest, which finishes on Sunday. “I want to do everything I can to make people feel secure,” she said.

There are signs and police posters in German and English around the tent where the Teufelsrad is located that warn against filming under people’s skirts. But Polaczy, 80, said it was difficult to control everyone filming with smartphones.
A spokesperson for the Bavarian police told the BBC they have put up posters at the Oktoberfest warning against upskirting since 2025.
Police arrested a 45-year-old Swiss man for filming under a German woman’s dirndl at this year’s festival. In 2025 there were 10 arrests for upskirting and seven in 2024.

articles.title: COA flags DA over undistributed agri aid for Kristine victims
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) has flagged the Department of Agriculture (DA) for the failure of its Regional Field Office in the Bicol Region (RFO V) to distribute agricultural inputs to…

blocks.text: Published October 3, 2026 11:07pm

The Commission on Audit (COA) has flagged the Department of Agriculture (DA) for the failure of its Regional Field Office in the Bicol Region (RFO V) to distribute agricultural inputs to beneficiaries affected by Severe Tropical Storm Kristine and other storms.

In its 2025 annual audit report, COA said a review of the DA's quick response fund (QRF) showed that RFO V failed to distribute the agricultural inputs on time. The inputs were intended for beneficiaries under the Rice, Corn and High Value Crops Programs.

“Despite the procurement and delivery of various agricultural inputs, most items remained undistributed as of year-end, with several already delivered to RFO V or for delivery/distribution, yet reflected zero physical accomplishment, indicating delays in the actual distribution to intended beneficiaries,” COA said.
The QRF was intended to address the effects of Typhoons Kristine and Pepito in 2024, as well as Tropical Depression Crising.

“Despite the lapse of several months and the prior identification of affected beneficiaries, a significant portion of inputs remained undistributed as of year-end, indicating undue delays in the provision of assistance,” COA said.
COA noted that one of the reasons cited by RFO V for the delayed distribution was its attempt to align the distribution of the inputs with planting schedules, among other factors.
RFO V maintained that the situation did not constitute an actual delay, according to state auditors.
However, COA said this reasoning defeated the purpose of the QRF.

“While the Audit Team acknowledges the justification of Management, the delay in distribution to aid various farmers after a calamity is not aligned with the very concept of the QRF, which is to help normalize a community’s situation after a disaster by providing immediate assistance to those affected by calamities,” COA said.

Among the agricultural inputs that RFO V failed to distribute under the rice program were 15,000 bags of hybrid palay seeds, 45,000 liters of inorganic foliar fertilizer and 15,000 packs of inorganic foliar fertilizer.
Under the corn program, the regional office also failed to distribute 1,710 liters of herbicide, 1,710 kilograms of complete fertilizer and 1,140 liters of pesticide, among other inputs.
Severe Tropical Storm Kristine brought torrential rains and widespread flooding to parts of the Philippines in October 2024.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council reported that Kristine affected more than 7 million people and resulted in 139 casualties as of Oct. 30, 2024.
The successive storms that hit the country in late 2024 also caused billions of pesos in agricultural damage and losses.
The government initially estimated about P7.039 billion in agricultural damage and losses from the successive typhoons in several regions.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: ‘This can’t go on’: tens of thousands protest against housing crisis in Spain
articles.summary:
Demonstrators take to the streets of Madrid ⁠and other Spanish cities ⁠after ​new legislation fails to pass

Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Madrid ⁠and other…

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Madrid ⁠and other Spanish cities as they step up demands for action to tackle ⁠a mounting housing crisis ⁠after ​government measures were struck down by the opposition.

Demonstrators on Saturday waved posters calling for a general strike ⁠after the measures drawn up to address mass anger over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in ⁠Madrid, and other housing issues, were rejected in parliament on ​Friday.
Authorities said 70,000 people were protesting. Organisers put the figure at 500,000.

“It’s a shame,” Nando ‌de Anguulo, 26, ‌who joined the protest in Madrid, told Reuters. “It only proves that it ‌is us the people who have to adapt to the political parties, and not the politicians to what the people want, and this can’t go on like that.”

Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, may call a snap election for November after the ‌legislation failed to pass, Spanish media reported on Friday, and would be watching the strength of Saturday’s ​protests before making a decision.

blocks.caption: Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of Madrid. Photograph: Alejandro Martinez Velez/Reuters

blocks.text: The demonstrations have dominated the national conversation, breathing new life into Sánchez’s beleaguered government and shifting attention away from the lingering impact of recent events in Ceuta.
Protests on Saturday were peaceful in 50 Spanish cities. In the south-eastern city of Valencia, demonstrators clashed with police who fired rubber bullets and teargas ⁠to break up the protests.
About 30 people managed to get inside ​the City ​of Arts and Sciences, a ​landmark cultural building in the city, before they were ​ousted by ‌police.

One protester in Madrid, Marcos Sainz, a librarian aged 26, said he used to rent a two-bedroom apartment with friends for a monthly rent of 900 euros ($1,000) but that a one-bedroom flat often now cost 1,000 euros – or half the median monthly salary in the capital.
He told AFP he would protest rental spikes “until someone dares to regulate it all as (otherwise) we’ll all have to leave Madrid and that would be a shame as I am from Madrid”.

Javier, 31, a solar panel installer, said: “We are demanding a fundamental right: decent housing, stability and conditions allowing us to construct a decent life project.” He added: “I spend half of my salary on a tiny room”.

“What we are feeling in the streets is a new energy that we haven’t seen in a long time, an energy that is showing that eight days of people power can achieve more than eight years of progressive government,” Valeria Racu, one of the spokespeople of the Tenants’ Union organising the protest, said in a statement.
“Now begins real politics – politics which has always belonged to the people and which will return once and for all to the streets,” she said.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Protesters clash with police during the demonstration in Valencia. Photograph: Kai Forsterling/EPA

blocks.text: On Friday, Sánchez’s Socialist-led coalition put forward two decrees that included a range of measures aimed at improving access to housing, from a ban on evictions until 2030 to the regulation of temporary lettings and lettings by room.
Despite the anger of the protesters outside parliament, the conservative People’s party, the far-right Vox and the Catalan pro-independence party Junts voted against both decrees.

The People’s party said it had voted in line with its belief that building, rather than regulating, was the best way to address the crisis. “Housing doesn’t become more affordable through decrees; it becomes more affordable by building ​more homes,” said the lawmaker Juan Bravo.

blocks.caption: A demonstrator holds up a sign reading ‘Right to a Roof’ on Plaza de Espana in Madrid. Photograph: Javier Soriano/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: News of the package’s rejection was met with boos and cries of “shame” outside. “Your profits, our misery,” the protesters chanted.

The long-simmering anger at soaring housing costs boiled over late last month, when 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who uses a wheelchair, was evicted from the home she had lived in for 70 years. The octogenarian said she was unable to afford the 230% rent hike demanded by the investment fund that bought her apartment.
Reuters and AFP contributed to this report.
